bio: One of the sons of Eli, the high priest (1 Sam. 1:3; 2:12). He and his brother Hophni were guilty of great crimes, for which destruction came on the house of Eli (31). He died in battle with the Philistines (1 Sam. 4:4, 11);

name: Priscilla
bio: The wife of Aquila (Acts 18:2), who is never mentioned without her. Her name sometimes takes the precedence of his (Rom. 16:3; 2 Tim. 4:19). She took part with Aquila (q.v.) in insturcting Apollos (Acts 18:26).

name: Ram
bio: The son of Hezron, and one of the ancestors of the royal line (Ruth 4:19). The margin of 1 Chr. 2:9, also Matt. 1:3, 4 and Luke 3:33, have “Aram.”

name: Reuel
bio: A son of Esau and Bashemath (Gen. 36:4, 10; 1 Chr. 1:35).

name: Salmon
bio: Shady; or Zalmon (q.v.), a hill covered with dark forests, south of Shechem, from which Abimelech and his men gathered wood to burn that city (Judg. 9:48). In Ps. 68:14 the change from war to peace is likened to snow on the dark mountain, as some interpret the expression.

name: Serug
bio: Branch, the father of Nahor (Gen. 11:20-23); called Saruch in Luke 3:35.

name: Shishak
bio: '=Sheshonk I., king of Egypt. His reign was one of great national success, and a record of his wars and conquests adorns the portico of what are called the “Bubastite kings” at Karnak, the ancient Thebes. Among these conquests is a record of that of Judea.

name: Tilgath-pilneser
bio: An Assyrian king. It has been a question whether he was identical with Tiglath-pileser III. (q.v.), or was his predecessor. The weight of evidence is certainly in favour of their identity.

name: Zechariah
bio: A prophet of Judah, the eleventh of the twelve minor prophets. Like Ezekiel, he was of priestly extraction. He describes himself (1:1) as “the son of Berechiah.” In Ezra 5:1 and 6:14 he is called “the son of Iddo,” who was properly his grandfather.

name: Zephaniah
bio: The son of Maaseiah, the “second priest” in the reign of Zedekiah, often mentioned in Jeremiah as having been sent from the king to inquire (Jer.

name: Abidan
bio: Father of judgment; judge, head of the tribe of Benjamin at the Exodus (Num. 1:11; 2:22).

name: Abiel
bio: The son of Zeror and father of Ner, who was the grandfather of Saul (1 Sam. 14:51; 1 Chr. 8:33; 9:39). In 1 Sam. 9:1, he is called the “father,” probably meaning the grandfather, of Kish.

name: Abinadab
bio: One of Saul’s sons, who peristed with his father in the battle of Gilboa (1 Sam. 31:2; 1 Chr. 10:2).

name: Abishag
bio: Father of (i.e., “given to”) error, a young woman of Shunem, distinguished for her beauty. She was chosen to minister to David in his old age. She became his wife (1 Kings 1:3, 4, 15).

name: Adoniram
bio: One who was “over the tribute;” i.e., “over the levy.” He was stoned by the Israelites after they had revolted from Rehoboam (2 Chr. 10:18). Called also Adoram (2 Sam. 20:24) and Adoniram (1 Kings 4:6).

name: Agag
bio: Another king of the Amalekites whom Saul spared unlawfully, but whom Samuel on his arrival in the camp of Saul ordered, in retributive justice (Judg. 1), to be brought out and cut in pieces (1 Sam. 15:8-33. Comp. Ex. 17:11; Num. 14:45).

name: Ahira
bio: Brother of evil = unlucky, or my brother is friend, chief of the tribe of Naphtali at the Exodus (Num. 1:15; 2:29).

name: Ahitub
bio: The son of Phinehas. On the death of his grandfather Eli he succeeded to the office of high priest, and was himself succeeded by his son Ahijah (1 Sam. 14:3; 22:9, 11, 12, 20).

name: Ahitub
bio: The father of Zadok, who was made high priest by Saul after the extermination of the family of Ahimelech (1 Chr. 6:7, 8; 2 Sam. 8:17).

name: Aholiab
bio: Tent of the father, an artist of the tribe of Dan, appointed to the work of preparing materials for the tabernacle (Ex. 31:6; 35:34; 36:1, 2; 38:23).

name: Aholibah
bio: My tent is in her, the name of an imaginary harlot, applied symbolically to Jerusalem, because she had abandoned the worship of the true God and given herself up to the idolatries of foreign nations. (Ezek. 23:4, 11, 22, 36, 44).

name: Aholibamah
bio: Jewess, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and one of Esau’s wives (Gen. 26:34), elsewhere called Aholibamah (36:2-14).

name: Akkub
bio: A Levite who kept the gate of the temple after the return from Babylon (1 Chr. 9:17; Ezra 2:42; Neh. 7:45).

name: Ammishaddai
bio: People of the Almighty, the father of Ahiezer, who was chief of the Danites at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:12; 2:25). This is one of the few names compounded with the name of God, Shaddai, “Almighty.”

name: Ananias (Disciple at Damascus)
bio: A Christian at Damascus (Acts 9:10). He became Paul’s instructor; but when or by what means he himself became a Christian we have no information. He was “a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt” at Damascus (22:12).

name: Aristarchus
bio: Best ruler, native of Thessalonica (Acts 20:4), a companion of Paul (Acts 19:29; 27:2). He was Paul’s “fellow-prisoner” at Rome (Col. 4:10; Philemon 1:24).

name: Asshur
bio: Second son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17). He went from the land of Shinar and built Nineveh, etc. (Gen. 10:11, 12). He probably gave his name to Assyria, which is the usual translation of the word, although the form Asshur is sometimes retained (Num. 24:22, 24; Ezek.

name: Azariah
bio: The original name of Abed-nego (Dan. 1:6, 7, 11, 16). He was of the royal family of Judah, and with his other two companions remarkable for his personal beauty and his intelligence as well as piety.

name: Benaiah
bio: A musical Levite (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

name: Beriah
bio: One of Asher’s four sons, and father of Heber (Gen. 46:17).

name: Bildad
bio: Son of contention, one of Job’s friends. He is called “the Shuhite,” probably as belonging to Shuah, a district in Arabia, in which Shuah, the sixth son of Abraham by Keturah, settled (Gen. 25:2).

name: Chedorlaomer
bio: (= Khudur-Lagamar of the inscriptions), king of Elam. Many centuries before the age of Abraham, Canaan and even the Sinaitic peninsula had been conquered by Babylonian kings, and in the time of Abraham himself Babylonia was ruled by a dynasty which claimed sovereignity over Syria…

name: Daughter of Pharaoh
bio: The wife of Solomon (1 Kings 3:1). This is the first reference since the Exodus to any connection of Israel with Egypt.

name: Diana
bio: So called by the Romans; called Artemis by the Greeks, the “great” goddess worshipped among heathen nations under various modifications. Her most noted temple was that at Ephesus. It was built outside the city walls, and was one of the seven wonders of the ancient world.

name: Dishan
bio: Antelope, the youngest son of Seir the Horite, head of one of the tribes of Idumaea (Gen. 36:21, 28, 30).

name: Ebed
bio: Slave, the father of Gaal, in whom the men of Shechem “put confidence” in their conspiracy against Abimelech (Judg. 9:26, 26, 30, 31).

name: Ebiasaph
bio: Father of gathering; the gatherer, the youngest of the three sons of Korah the Levite, head of a family of Korhites (Ex. 6:24); called Ebisaph (1 Chr. 6:37).

name: Eliab
bio: A Reubenite, son of Pallu (Num. 16:1, 12; 26:8, 9; Deut. 11:6).

name: Ezer
bio: One of the sons of Seir, the native princes, “dukes,” of Mount Hor (Gen. 36:21, 27).

name: Gamaliel
bio: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh at the census at Sinai (Num. 1:10; 2:20; 7:54, 59).

name: Gershom
bio: The elder of the two sons of Moses born to him in Midian (Ex. 2:22; 18:3). On his way to Egypt with his family, in obedience to the command of the Lord, Moses was attacked by a sudden and dangerous illness (4:24-26), which Zipporah his wife believed to have been sent because he h…

name: Gomer (son of Japheth)
bio: The eldest son of Japheth, and father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah (Gen. 10:2, 3), whose descendants formed the principal branch of the population of South-eastern Europe.

name: Hadad
bio: One of “the king’s seed in Edom.” He fled into Egypt, where he married the sister of Pharaoh’s wife (1 Kings 11:14-22). He became one of Solomon’s adversaries. Hadad, sharp, (a different name in Hebrew from the preceding), one of the sons of Ishmael (1 Chr. 1:30).

name: Haggith
bio: Festive; the dancer, a wife of David and the mother of Adonijah (2 Sam. 3:4; 1 Kings 1:5, 11; 2:13; 1 Chr. 3:2), who, like Absalom, was famed for his beauty.

name: Hammedatha
bio: Father of Haman, designated usually “the Agagite” (Esther 3:1, 10; 8:5).

name: Hanani
bio: A prophet who was sent to rebuke king Asa for entering into a league with Benhadad I., king of Syria, against Judah (2 Chr. 16:1-10). He was probably the father of the prophet Jehu (1 Kings 16:7).

name: Haran (brother of Abraham)
bio: Heb. haran; i.e., “mountaineer.” The eldest son of Terah, brother of Abraham and Nahor, and father of Lot, Milcah, and Iscah. He died before his father (Gen. 11:27), in Ur of the Chaldees.

name: Harim
bio: The head of the second course of priests (1 Chr. 24:8).

name: Helon
bio: Strong, father of Eliab, who was “captain of the children of Zebulun” (Num. 1:9; 2:7).

name: Hepher
bio: The youngest son of Gilead (Num. 26:32; 27:1).

name: Hezron
bio: One of the sons of Reuben (Gen. 46:9; Ex. 6:14).

name: Hilkiah
bio: The father of Eliakim (2 Kings 18:18, 26, 37).

name: Hiram
bio: The “master workman” whom Hiram sent to Solomon. He was the son of a widow of Dan, and of a Tyrian father. In 2 Chr.

name: Hophni
bio: Pugilist or client, one of the two sons of Eli, the high priest (1 Sam. 1:3; 2:34), who, because he was “very old,” resigned to them the active duties of his office. By their scandalous conduct they brought down a curse on their father’s house (2:22, 12-27, 27-36; 3:11-14).

name: Immer
bio: The head of the sixteenth priestly order (1 Chr. 24:14).

name: James (Son of Alphaeus)
bio: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature. He is mentioned along with the other apostles (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15).

name: Jason
bio: He that will cure, the host of Paul and Silas in Thessalonica. The Jews assaulted his house in order to seize Paul, but failing to find him, they dragged Jason before the ruler of the city (Acts 17:5-9). He was apparently one of the kinsmen of Paul (Rom.

name: Jehu
bio: The son of Hanani, a prophet of Judah (1 Kings 16:1, 7; 2 Chr. 19:2; 20:34), who pronounced the sentence of God against Baasha, the king of Israel.

name: Kenaz
bio: Caleb’s younger brother, and father of Othniel (Josh. 15:17), whose family was of importance in Israel down to the time of David (1 Chr. 27:15). Some think that Othniel (Judg. 1:13), and not Kenaz, was Caleb’s brother.

name: Lebbaeus Thaddaeus
bio: Breast, the name of one of the apostles (Mark 3:18), called “Lebbaeus” in Matt. 10:3, and in Luke 6:16, “Judas the brother of James;” while John (14:22), probably referring to the same person, speaks of “Judas, not Iscariot.” These different names all designate the same person, v…

name: Lotan
bio: Coverer, one of the sons of Seir, the Horite (Gen. 36:20, 29).

name: Magog
bio: Region of Gog, the second of the “sons” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5). In Ezekiel (38:2; 39:6) it is the name of a nation, probably some Scythian or Tartar tribe descended from Japheth. They are described as skilled horsemen, and expert in the use of the bow.

name: Mattithiah
bio: One of the sons of Jeduthun (1 Chr. 25:3, 21).

name: Meshelemiah
bio: Friendship of Jehovah, a Levite of the family of the Korhites, called also Shelemiah (1 Chr. 9:21; 26:1, 2, 9, 14). He was a temple gate-keeper in the time of David.

name: Michael
bio: The title given to one of the chief angels (Dan. 10:13, 21; 12:1). He had special charge of Israel as a nation. He disputed with Satan (Jude 1:9) about the body of Moses.

name: Nathan
bio: A son of David, by Bathsheba (2 Sam. 5:14), whose name appears in the genealogy of Mary, the mother of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

name: Nebajoth
bio: Ishmael’s eldest son (Gen. 25:13), and the prince of an Israelitish tribe (16). He had a sister, Mahalath, who was one of Esau’s wives (Gen. 28:9; 36:3).

name: Nehemiah
bio: The son of Hachaliah (Neh. 1:1), and probably of the tribe of Judah. His family must have belonged to Jerusalem (Neh. 2:3). He was one of the “Jews of the dispersion,” and in his youth was appointed to the important office of royal cup-bearer at the palace of Shushan.

name: Nethaneel
bio: The son of Zuar, chief of the tribe of Issachar at the Exodus (Num. 1:8; 2:5).

name: Nicodemus
bio: The people is victor, a Pharisee and a member of the Sanhedrin. He is first noticed as visiting Jesus by night (John 3:1-21) for the purpose of learning more of his doctrines, which our Lord then unfolded to him, giving prominence to the necessity of being “born again.” He is nex…

name: Nimshi
bio: Saved. Jehu was “the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi” (2 Kings 9:2; comp. 1 Kings 19:16).

name: Pagiel
bio: God allots, a prince of the tribe of Asher (Num. 1:13), in the wilderness.

name: Pallu
bio: Separated, the second son of Reuben (1 Chr. 5:3); called Phallu, Gen. 46:9. He was the father of the Phalluites (Ex. 6:14; Num. 26:5, 8).

name: Pedahzur
bio: Rock of redemption, the father of Gamaliel and prince of Manasseh at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:10; 2:20).

name: Pharaoh
bio: The “new king who knew not Joseph” (Ex. 1:8-22) has been generally supposed to have been Aahmes I., or Amosis, as he is called by Josephus.

name: Pharaoh
bio: Pharaoh, in whom Hezekiah put his trust in his war against Sennacherib (2 Kings 18:21).

name: Rehum
bio: One of “the children of the province” who returned from the Captivity (Ezra 2:2); the same as “Nehum” (Neh. 7:7).

name: Seraiah
bio: A ruler of the temple (Neh. 11:11).

name: Shallum
bio: A keeper of the gate in the reign of David (1 Chr. 9:17).

name: Shammah
bio: One of the sons of Jesse (1 Sam. 16:9). He is also called Shimeah (2 Sam. 13:3) and Shimma (1 Chr. 2:13).

name: Shemaiah
bio: A prophet in the reign of Rehoboam (1 Kings 12:22-24).

name: Shobal
bio: The second son of Seir the Horite; one of the Horite “dukes” (Gen. 36:20).

name: Sibbechai
bio: The Lord sustains, one of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:29), general of the eighth division of the army (27:11). He slew the giant Saph in the battle of Gob (2 Sam. 21:18; R.V., “Sibbechai”). Called also Mebunnai (23:27).

name: Talmon
bio: A Levite porter (1 Chr. 9:17; Neh. 11:19).

name: Tirzah
bio: The youngest of Zelophehad’s five daughters (Num. 26:33; Josh. 17:3).

name: Tychicus
bio: Chance, an Asiatic Christian, a “faithful minister in the Lord” (Eph. 6:21, 22), who, with Trophimus, accompanied Paul on a part of his journey from Macedonia to Jerusalem (Acts 20:4). He is alluded to also in Col. 4:7, Titus 3:12, and 2 Tim.

name: Urijah
bio: A high priest in the time of Ahaz (2 Kings 16:10-16), at whose bidding he constructed an idolatrous altar like one the king had seen at Damascus, to be set up instead of the brazen altar.

name: Zebul
bio: Habitation, the governor of Shechem under Abimelech (Judg. 9:28, 30, 36). He informed his master of the intention of the people of Shechem to transfer their allegiance to the Hivite tribe of Hamor.

name: Zedekiah
bio: The son of Chenaanah, a false prophet in the days of Ahab (1 Kings 22:11, 24; 2 Chr. 18:10, 23).

name: Zurishaddai
bio: Rock of the Almighty, the father of Shelumiel, who was chief of the tribe of Simeon when Israel was encamped at Sinai (Num. 1:6; 2:12).

name: Abiezer
bio: The second of the three sons of Hammoleketh, the sister of Gilead. He was the grandson of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:18). From his family Gideon sprang (Josh. 17:2; comp. Judg. 6:34; 8:2). He was also called Jeezer (Num. 26:30).

name: Abinadab
bio: A Levite of Kirjath-jearim, in whose house the ark of the covenant was deposited after having been brought back from the land of the Philistines (1 Sam. 7:1). It remained there twenty years, till it was at length removed by David (1 Sam. 7:1, 2; 1 Chr. 13:7).

name: Abinoam
bio: Father of kindness, the father of Barak (Judg. 4:6; 5:1).

name: Abishua
bio: The son of Phinehas the high priest (1 Chr. 6:4, 5, 50; Ezra 7:5).

name: Achsah
bio: Anklet, Caleb’s only daughter (1 Chr. 2:49). She was offered in marriage to the man who would lead an attack on the city of Debir, or Kirjath-sepher. This was done by Othniel (q.v.), who accordingly obtained her as his wife (Josh. 15:16-19; Judg. 1:9-15).

name: Ahaz
bio: A grandson of Jonathan (1 Chr. 8:35; 9:42).

name: Alphaeus
bio: The father of James the Less, the apostle and writer of the epistle (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15; Acts 1:13), and the husband of Mary (John 19:25). The Hebrew form of this name is Cleopas, or Clopas (q.v.).

name: Amorite
bio: Highlanders, or hillmen, the name given to the descendants of one of the sons of Canaan (Gen. 14:7), called Amurra or Amurri in the Assyrian and Egyptian inscriptions.

name: Annas
bio: Was high priest A.D. 7-14. In A.D. 25 Caiaphas, who had married the daughter of Annas (John 18:13), was raised to that office, and probably Annas was now made president of the Sanhedrim, or deputy or coadjutor of the high priest, and thus was also called high priest along with Ca…

name: Azel
bio: Noble, a descendant of king Saul (1 Chr. 8:37; 9:43, 44).

name: Baalhanan
bio: A king of Edom, son of Achbor (Gen. 36:38, 39; 1 Chr. 1:49, 50).

name: Baal-zebub
bio: Fly-lord, the god of the Philistines at Ekron (2 Kings 1:2, 3, 16). This name was given to the god because he was supposed to be able to avert the plague of flies which in that region was to be feared. He was consulted by Ahaziah as to his recovery.

name: Baanah
bio: One of the two sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, a captain in Saul’s army. He and his brother Rechab assassinated Ishbosheth (2 Sam. 4:2), and were on this account slain by David, and their mutilated bodies suspended over the pool at Hebron (5, 6, 12).

name: Bartholomew
bio: Son of Tolmai, one of the twelve apostles (Matt. 10:3; Acts 1:13); generally supposed to have been the same as Nathanael. In the synoptic gospels Philip and Bartholomew are always mentioned together, while Nathanael is never mentioned;

name: Bela
bio: The son of Beor, and a king of Edom (Gen. 36:32, 33; 1 Chr. 1:43).

name: Ben-hadad
bio: King of Damascus, and successor of his father Hazael on the throne of Syria (2 Kings 13:3, 4). His misfortunes in war are noticed by Amos (1:4).

name: Carmi
bio: The last named of the four sons of Reuben (Gen. 46:9).

name: Chenaanah
bio: The father of Zedekiah (1 Kings 22:11, 24).

name: Doeg
bio: Fearful, an Edomite, the chief overseer of Saul’s flocks (1 Sam. 21:7). At the command of Saul he slew the high priest Ahimelech (q.v.) at Nob, together with all the priests to the number of eighty-five persons. (Comp. Ps. 52, title.)

name: Eglon
bio: Chieftain or king of one of the Moabite tribes (Judg. 3:12-14). Having entered into an alliance with Ammon and Amalek, he overran the trans-Jordanic region, and then crossing the Jordan, seized on Jericho, the “city of palm trees,” which had been by this time rebuilt, but not as…

name: Elah
bio: The son and successor of Baasha, king of Israel (1 Kings 16:8-10). He was killed while drunk by Zimri, one of the captains of his chariots, and was the last king of the line of Baasha. Thus was fullfilled the prophecy of Jehu (6, 7, 11-14).

name: Elah
bio: The father of Hoshea, the last king of Israel (2 Kings 15:30; 17:1).

name: Eliashib
bio: A high priest in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah (Neh. 12:22, 23). He rebuilt the eastern city wall (3:1), his own mansion being in that quarter, on the ridge Ophel (3:20, 21). His indulgence of Tobiah the Ammonite provoked the indignation of Nehemiah (13:4, 7).

name: Eliezer
bio: One of the two sons of Moses, born during his sojourn in Midian (Ex. 18:4; 1 Chr. 23:15, 17). He remained with his mother and brother Gershom with Jethro when Moses returned to Egypt. (Ex. 18:4). They were restored to Moses when Jethro heard of his departure out of Egypt.

name: Ephratah
bio: The second wife of Caleb, the son of Hezron, mother of Hur, and grandmother of Caleb, who was one of those that were sent to spy the land (1 Chr. 2:19, 50).

name: Eve
bio: Life; living, the name given by Adam to his wife (Gen. 3:20; 4:1). The account of her creation is given in Gen. 2:21, 22. The Creator, by declaring that it was not good for man to be alone, and by creating for him a suitable companion, gave sanction to monogamy.

name: Gabriel
bio: Champion of God, used as a proper name to designate the angel who was sent to Daniel (8:16) to explain the vision of the ram and the he-goat, and to communicate the prediction of the seventy weeks (Dan. 9:21-27).

name: Gemariah
bio: The son of Shaphan, and one of the Levites of the temple in the time of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:10; 2 Kings 22:12). Baruch read aloud to the people from Gemariah’s chamber, and again in the hearing of Gemariah and other scribes, the prophecies of Jeremiah (Jer.

name: Gera
bio: The father of Shimei, who so grossly abused David (2 Sam. 16:5; 19:16, 18).

name: Geshem
bio: Or Gashmu, firmness, probably chief of the Arabs south of Palestine, one of the enemies of the Jews after the return from Babylon (Neh. 2:19; 6:1, 2). He united with Sanballat and Tobiah in opposing the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem.

name: Hadad
bio: An Edomite king who defeated the Midianites (Gen. 36:35; 1 Chr. 1:46).

name: Hanameel
bio: Whom God has graciously given, the cousin of Jeremiah, to whom he sold the field he possessed in Anathoth, before the siege of Jerusalem (Jer. 32:6-12).

name: Hashabiah
bio: One of the chief priests in the time of Ezra (Ezra 8:24).

name: Hatach
bio: Verity, one of the eunuchs or chamberlains in the palace of Ahasuerus (Esther 4:5, 6, 9, 10).

name: Heber
bio: The Kenite (Judg. 4:11, 17; 5:24), a descendant of Hobab. His wife Jael received Sisera (q.v.) into her tent and then killed him.

name: Herodias
bio: (Matt. 14:3-11; Mark 6:17-28; Luke 3:19), the daughter of Aristobulus and Bernice. While residing at Rome with her husband Herod Philip I. and her daughter, Herod Antipas fell in with her during one of his journeys to that city.

name: Hoglah
bio: Partridge, one of the daughters of Zelophehad the Gileadite, to whom portions were assigned by Moses (Num. 26:33; 27:1; 36:11).

name: Hosah
bio: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 16:38).

name: Imla
bio: Replenisher, the father of Micaiah the prophet (2 Chr. 18:7, 8).

name: Jaalam
bio: Concealer, the second of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14).

name: Jachin
bio: The fourth son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10), called also Jarib (1 Chr. 4:24).

name: Jedaiah
bio: A priest in Jerusalem after the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

name: Jehoshaphat
bio: Son of Ahilud, “recorder” or annalist under David and Solomon (2 Sam. 8:16), a state officer of high rank, chancellor or vizier of the kingdom.

name: Jeiel
bio: One of the Levites who took part in praising God on the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 16:5).

name: Jemuel
bio: One of Simeon’s five sons (1 Chr. 4:24), called also Jemuel (Gen. 46:10).

name: Jeshua
bio: Head of the ninth priestly order (Ezra 2:36); called also Jeshuah (1 Chr. 24:11).

name: Jether
bio: The father of Amasa, David’s general (1 Kings 2:5, 32); called Ithra (2 Sam. 17:25).

name: Jeush
bio: The oldest of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14, 18).

name: Jezaniah
bio: A Maachathite (2 Kings 25:23; Jer. 40:8; 42:1). He is also called Azariah (Jer. 43:2).

name: Jobab
bio: King of Edom, succeeded Bela (Gen. 36:33, 34).

name: Joel
bio: The oldest of Samuel’s two sons appointed by him as judges in Beersheba (1 Sam. 8:2).

name: Joiarib
bio: The founder of one of the courses of the priests (Neh. 11:10).

name: Jonas
bio: The father of the apostles Peter (John 21:15-17) and Andrew; but the reading should be (also in 1:42), as in the Revised Version, “John,” instead of Jonas.

name: Josiah
bio: Common in later times among the Jews in Palestine (Matt. 23:37; Luke 13:34). It is noticeable that this familiar bird is only mentioned in these passages in connection with our Lord’s lamentation over the impenitence of Jerusalem.

name: Jotham
bio: The youngest of Gideon’s seventy sons. He escaped when the rest were put to death by the order of Abimelech (Judg. 9:5). When “the citizens of Shechem and the whole house of Millo” were gathered together “by the plain of the pillar” (i.e., the stone set up by Joshua, 24:26;

name: Keturah
bio: Incense, the wife of Abraham, whom he married probably after Sarah’s death (Gen. 25:1-6), by whom he had six sons, whom he sent away into the east country. Her nationality is unknown. She is styled “Abraham’s concubine” (1 Chr. 1:32).

name: Korah
bio: The third son of Esau, by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:14; 1 Chr. 1:35).

name: Lamech (descendant of Cain)
bio: The fifth in descent from Cain. He was the first to violate the primeval ordinance of marriage (Gen. 4:18-24). His address to his two wives, Adah and Zillah (4:23, 24), is the only extant example of antediluvian poetry.

name: Lydia
bio: A woman of Thyatira, a “seller of purple,” who dwelt in Philippi (Acts 16:14, 15). She was not a Jewess but a proselyte. The Lord opened her heart as she heard the gospel from the lips of Paul (16:13). She thus became the first in Europe who embraced Christianity.

name: Mahlah
bio: Disease, one of the five daughters of Zelophehad (Num. 27:1-11) who had their father’s inheritance, the law of inheritance having been altered in their favour.

name: Mahlon
bio: Sickly, the elder of Elimelech the Bethlehemite’s two sons by Naomi. He married Ruth and died childless (Ruth 1:2, 5; 4:9, 10), in the land of Moab.

name: Malchi-shua
bio: King of help, one of the four sons of Saul (1 Chr. 8:33). He perished along with his father in the battle of Gilboa (1 Sam. 31:2).

name: Merab
bio: Increase, the eldest of Saul’s two daughters (1 Sam. 14:49). She was betrothed to David after his victory over Goliath, but does not seem to have entered heartily into this arrangement (18:2, 17, 19).

name: Mizraim
bio: The dual form of matzor, meaning a “mound” or “fortress,” the name of a people descended from Ham (Gen. 10:6, 13; 1 Chr. 1:8, 11). It was the name generally given by the Hebrews to the land of Egypt (q.v.), and may denote the two Egypts, the Upper and the Lower.

name: Moza
bio: The son of Zimri, of the posterity of Saul (1 Chr. 8:36, 37; 9:42, 43).

name: Nadab
bio: The son and successor of Jeroboam, the king of Israel (1 Kings 14:20). While engaged with all Israel in laying siege to Gibbethon, a town of southern Dan (Josh.

name: Nimrod
bio: Firm, a descendant of Cush, the son of Ham. He was the first who claimed to be a “mighty one in the earth.” Babel was the beginning of his kingdom, which he gradually enlarged (Gen. 10:8-10).

name: Noah (daughter of Zelophehad)
bio: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death.

name: Oreb
bio: Raven, a prince of Midian, who, being defeated by Gideon and put to straits, was slain along with Zeeb (Judg. 7:20-25). Many of the Midianites perished along with him (Ps. 83:9; Isa. 10:26).

name: Pahath-moab
bio: Governor of Moab, a person whose descendants returned from the Captivity and assisted in rebuilding Jerusalem (Ezra 2:6; 8:4; 10:30).

name: Pharaoh (during Abraham's Journey)
bio: The Pharaoh who was on the throne when Abram went down into Egypt (Gen. 12:10-20) was probably one of the Hyksos, or “shepherd kings.” The Egyptians called the nomad tribes of Syria Shasu, “plunderers,” their king or chief Hyk, and hence the name of those invaders who conquered t…

name: Rechab
bio: One of Ishbosheth’s “captains of bands” or leaders of predatory troops (2 Sam. 4:2).

name: Rehum
bio: The “chancellor” of Artaxerxes, who sought to stir him up against the Jews (Ezra 4:8-24) and prevent the rebuilding of the walls and the temple of Jerusalem.

name: Rizpah
bio: Coal; hot stone, the daughter of Aiah, and one of Saul’s concubines. She was the mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth (2 Sam. 3:7; 21:8, 10, 11).

name: Seir
bio: A Horite; one of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:20-30).

name: Seraiah
bio: A priest of the days of Jehoiakim (Neh. 12:1, 12).

name: Shallum
bio: The son of Jabesh, otherwise unknown. He “conspired against Zachariah, and smote him before the people, and slew him, and reigned in his stead” (2 Kings 15:10). He reigned only “a month of days in Samaria” (15:13, marg.).

name: Shaphat
bio: The father of Elisha (1 Kings 19:16-19).

name: Shaul
bio: A king of Edom (Gen. 36:37, 38); called Shaul in 1 Chr. 1:48.

name: Shavsha
bio: (“Seraiah,” 2 Sam. 8:17; “Shisha,” 1 Kings 4:3), one of David’s secretaries (1 Chr. 18:16).

name: Shethar-boznai
bio: Star of splendour, a Persian officer who vainly attempted to hinder the rebuilding of the temple (Ezra 5:3, 6; 6:6, 13).

name: Shimshai
bio: The shining one, or sunny, the secretary of Rehum the chancellor, who took part in opposing the rebuilding of the temple after the Captivity (Ezra 4:8, 9, 17-23).

name: Shobach
bio: Poured out, the “captain of the host of Hadarezer” when he mustered his vassals and tributaries from beyond “the river Euphrates” (2 Sam. 10:15-18); called also Shophach (1 Chr. 19:16).

name: Shobal
bio: One of the sons of Caleb, and a descendant of Hur (1 Chr. 2:50, 52; 4:1, 2).

name: Simon Zelotes
bio: One of the twelve apostles, called the Canaanite (Matt. 10:4; Mark 3:18). This word “Canaanite” does not mean a native of Canaan, but is derived from the Syriac word Kanean or Kaneniah, which was the name of a Jewish sect.

name: Simon the Sorcerer
bio: A sorcerer of great repute for his magical arts among the Samaritans (Acts 8:9-11). He afterwards became a professed convert to the faith under the preaching of Philip the deacon and evangelist (12, 13). His profession was, however, soon found to be hollow.

name: Simon the Tanner
bio: A Christian at Joppa, a tanner by trade, with whom Peter on one occasion lodged (Acts 9:43).

name: Tatnai
bio: Gift, a Persian governor (Heb. pehah, i.e., “satrap;” modern “pasha”) “on this side the river”, i.e., of the whole tract on the west of the Euphrates. This Hebrew title pehah is given to governors of provinces generally. It is given to Nehemiah (5:14) and to Zerubbabel (Hag.

name: Togarmah
bio: A son of Gomer, and grandson of Japheth (Gen. 10:3).

name: Toi
bio: A king of Hamath, who sent “Joram his son unto King David to salute him,” when he “heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer” (2 Sam. 8:9, 10). Called Tou (1 Chr. 18:9, 10).

name: Tola
bio: Eldest son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13).

name: Uzzi
bio: The son of Bukki, and a descendant of Aaron (1 Chr. 6:5, 51; Ezra 7:4).

name: Zabdi
bio: An ancestor of Achan (Josh. 7:1, 17, 18). He is probably the “Zimri” of 1 Chr. 2:6.

name: Zerah
bio: One of the sons of Simeon (Gen. 46:10; Ex. 6:15).

name: Zophar
bio: Chirping, one of Job’s friends who came to condole with him in his distress (Job 2:11. The LXX. render here “king of the Mineans” = Ma’in, Maonites, Judg. 10:12, in Southern Arabia). He is called a Naamathite, or an inhabitant of some unknown place called Naamah.

name: Abiezer
bio: One of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:27; comp. 1 Chr. 27:12).

name: Abigail
bio: The sister of David, and wife of Jether an Ishmaelite (1 Chr. 2:16, 17). She was the mother of Amasa (2 Sam. 17:25).

name: Abinadab
bio: The second of the eight sons of Jesse (1 Sam. 16:8). He was with Saul in the campaign against the Philistines in which Goliath was slain (1 Sam. 17:13).

name: Achbor
bio: An Edomitish king (Gen. 36:38; 1 Chr. 1:49).

name: Achbor
bio: The son of Micah, one of those whom Josiah sent to the prophetess Huldah to ascertain from her the meaning of the recently discovered book of the law (2 Chr. 34:20). He is called Achbor in 2 Kings 22:12.

name: Adah (wife of Lamech)
bio: The first of Lamech’s two wives, and the mother of Jabal and Jubal (Gen. 4:19, 20, 23).

name: Adin
bio: Ezra 8:6.

name: Adonikam
bio: Whom the Lord sets up, one of those “which came with Zerubbabel” (Ezra 2:13). His “children,” or retainers, to the number of 666, came up to Jerusalem (8:13).

name: Ahiman
bio: One of the three giant Anakim brothers whom Caleb and the spies saw in Mount Hebron (Num. 13:22) when they went in to explore the land. They were afterwards driven out and slain (Josh. 15:14; Judg. 1:10).

name: Ahio
bio: One of the sons of Abinadab the Levite. While Uzzah went by the side of the ark, he walked before it guiding the oxen which drew the cart on which it was carried, after having brought it from his father’s house in Gibeah (1 Chr. 13:7; 2 Sam. 6:3, 4).

name: Amaziah
bio: A priest of the golden calves at Bethel (Amos 7:10-17).

name: Ammiel
bio: The father of Machir of Lo-debar, in whose house Mephibosheth resided (2 Sam. 9:4, 5; 17:27).

name: Ananias (Husband of Sapphira)
bio: One of the members of the church at Jerusalem, who conspired with his wife Sapphira to deceive the brethren, and who fell down and immediately expired after he had uttered the falsehood (Acts 5:5).

name: Arad
bio: One of the sons of Beriah (1 Chr. 8:15).

name: Aram (son of Shem)
bio: The son of Shem (Gen. 10:22); according to Gen. 22:21, a grandson of Nahor. In Matt. 1:3, 4, and Luke 3:33, this word is the Greek form of Ram, the father of Amminadab (1 Chr. 2:10).

name: Artaxerxes
bio: The king who obstructed the rebuilding of the temple (Ezra 4:7). He was probably the Smerdis of profane history.

name: Asahiah
bio: The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg.

name: Asaph
bio: The “recorder” in the time of Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:18, 37).

name: Asenath
bio: An Egyptian name, meaning “gift of the sun-god”, daughter of Potipherah, priest of On or Heliopolis, wife of Joseph (Gen. 41:45). She was the mother of Manasseh and Ephraim (50-52; 46:20).

name: Ashkenaz
bio: One of the three sons of Gomer (Gen. 10:3), and founder of one of the tribes of the Japhetic race. They are mentioned in connection with Minni and Ararat, and hence their original seat must have been in Armenia (Jer.

name: Ashtoreth
bio: The moon goddess of the Phoenicians, representing the passive principle in nature, their principal female deity; frequently associated with the name of Baal, the sun-god, their chief male deity (Judg. 10:6; 1 Sam. 7:4; 12:10).

name: Augustus
bio: The cognomen of the first Roman emperor, C. Julius Caesar Octavianus, during whose reign Christ was born (Luke 2:1). His decree that “all the world should be taxed” was the divinely ordered occasion of Jesus’ being born, according to prophecy (Micah 5:2), in Bethlehem.

name: Ben-hadad
bio: Son of the preceding, also king of Syria. He was long engaged in war against Israel. He was murdered probably by Hazael, by whom he was succeeded (2 Kings 8:7-15), after a reign of some thirty years.

name: Berechiah
bio: Son of Shimea, and father of Asaph the musician (1 Chr. 6:39; 15:17).

name: Bernice
bio: Bearer of victory, the eldest daughter of Agrippa I., the Herod Agrippa of Acts 12:20. After the early death of her first husband she was married to her uncle Herod, king of Chalcis. After his death (A.D. 40) she lived in incestuous connection with her brother Agrippa II.

name: Bilgah
bio: A priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5, 18).

name: Carmi
bio: The son of Zimri, and the father of Achan (Josh. 7:1), “the troubler of Israel.”

name: Chilion
bio: The pining one, the younger son of Elimelech and Naomi, and husband of Orpah, Ruth’s sister (Ruth 1:2; 4:9).

name: Demas
bio: A companion and fellow-labourer of Paul during his first imprisonment at Rome (Philemon 1:24; Col. 4:14). It appears, however, that the love of the world afterwards mastered him, and he deserted the apostle (2 Tim. 4:10).

name: Demetrius
bio: A silversmith at Ephesus, whose chief occupation was to make “silver shrines for Diana” (q.v.), Acts 19:24, i.e., models either of the temple of Diana or of the statue of the goddess.

name: Dodo
bio: An Ahohite, father of Eleazar, who was one of David’s three heroes (2 Sam. 23:9; 1 Chr. 11:12). He was the same with Dodai mentioned in 1 Chr. 27:4.

name: Dorcas
bio: (in Greek called Dorcas), gazelle, a disciple at Joppa. She was distinguished for her alms-deeds and good works. Peter, who was sent for from Lydda on the occasion of her death, prayed over the dead body, and said, “Tabitha, arise.” And she opened her eyes and sat up;

name: Eleasah
bio: A descendant of king Saul (1 Chr. 8:37; 9:43).

name: Eleazar
bio: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 23:21, 22).

name: Eliada
bio: One of David’s sons born after his establishment in Jerusalem (2 Sam. 5:16).

name: Elihu
bio: The son of Tohu, and grandfather of Elkanah (1 Sam. 1:1). He is called also Eliel (1 Chr. 6:34) and Eliab (6:27).

name: Eliphalet
bio: God his deliverance, one of David’s sons (2 Sam. 5:16); called also Eliphelet (1 Chr. 3:8).

name: Elishua
bio: God his salvation, a son of David, 2 Sam. 5:15 = Elishama, 1 Chr. 3:6.

name: Epaphras
bio: Lovely, spoken of by Paul (Col. 1:7; 4:12) as “his dear fellow-servant,” and “a faithful minister of Christ.” He was thus evidently with him at Rome when he wrote to the Colossians. He was a distinguished disciple, and probably the founder of the Colossian church.

name: Erastus
bio: A companion of Paul at Ephesus, who was sent by him along with Timothy into Macedonia (Acts 19:22). Corinth was his usual place of abode (2 Tim. 4:20); but probably he may have been the same as the preceding.

name: Ezra
bio: A priest among those that returned to Jerusalem under Zerubabel (Neh. 12:1).

name: Gallio
bio: The elder brother of Seneca the philosopher, who was tutor and for some time minister of the emperor Nero. He was “deputy”, i.e., proconsul, as in Revised Version, of Achaia, under the emperor Claudius, when Paul visited Corinth (Acts 18:12).

name: Gareb
bio: One of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:38), an Ithrite.

name: Gera
bio: The father of Ehud the judge (Judg. 3:15).

name: Hadad
bio: One of the Edomitish kings (Gen. 36:39) about the time of Saul. Called also Hadad (1 Chr. 1:50, 51). It is probable that in these cases Hadar may be an error simply of transcription for Hadad.

name: Hamul
bio: Spared, one of the sons of Pharez, son of Judah (1 Chr. 2:5). His descendants are called Hamulites (Num. 26:21).

name: Hamutal
bio: Kinsman of the dew, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, wife of king Josiah, and mother of king Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:31), also of king Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:18).

name: Hegai
bio: Eunuch, had charge of the harem of Ahasuerus (Esther 2:8).

name: Heleb
bio: Fatness, one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:29).

name: Helez
bio: One of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:26).

name: Hodijah
bio: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra in expounding the law (Neh. 8:7; 9:5).

name: Hosea
bio: Salvation, the son of Beeri, and author of the book of prophecies bearing his name. He belonged to the kingdom of Israel. “His Israelitish origin is attested by the peculiar, rough, Aramaizing diction, pointing to the northern part of Palestine;

name: Huram
bio: Generally “Huram,” one of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 8:5).

name: Ibhar
bio: Chosen, one of David’s sons (1 Chr. 3:6; 2 Sam. 5:15).

name: Iddo
bio: Lovely. A prophet of Judah who wrote the history of Rehoboam and Abijah (2 Chr. 12:15). He has been identified with Oded (2 Chr. 15:1).

name: Ira
bio: A Tekoite, one of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:26).

name: Jabesh
bio: The father of Shallum (2 Kings 15:10, 13, 14), who usurped the throne of Israel on the death of Zachariah.

name: Jahzeel
bio: Allotted by God, the first of the sons of Naphtali (Gen. 46:24).

name: Japhia
bio: One of the sons of David (2 Sam. 5:15), born in Jerusalem.

name: Jashub
bio: The third of Issachar’s four sons (1 Chr. 7:1); called also Job (Gen. 46:13).

name: Jedaiah
bio: Knowing Jehovah. The chief of one of the courses of the priests (1 Chr. 24:7).

name: Jediael
bio: One of the sons of Benjamin, whose descendants numbered 17,200 warriors (1 Chr. 7:6, 10, 11).

name: Jehiel
bio: One of the Levites “of the second degree,” appointed to conduct the music on the occasion of the ark’s being removed to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

name: Jehudi
bio: A Jew, son of Nethaniah. He was sent by the princes to invite Baruch to read Jeremiah’s roll to them (Jer. 36:14, 21).

name: Jeremiah
bio: The father of Hamutal (2 Kings 23:31), the wife of Josiah.

name: Jeroham
bio: Father of Elkanah, and grandfather of the prophet Samuel (1 Sam. 1:1).

name: Joiakim
bio: (whom Jehovah has set up) = Jehoiakim, a high priest, the son and successor of Jeshua (Neh. 12:10, 12, 26).

name: Jokshan
bio: Snarer, the second son of Abraham and Keturah (Gen. 25:2, 3; 1 Chr. 1:32).

name: Judas Barsabas
bio: A Christian teacher, surnamed Barsabas. He was sent from Jerusalem to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas with the decision of the council (Acts 15:22, 27, 32). He was a “prophet” and a “chief man among the brethren.”

name: Jude
bio: '= Judas. Among the apostles there were two who bore this name, (1) Judas (Jude 1:1; Matt. 13:55; John 14:22; Acts 1:13), called also Lebbaeus or Thaddaeus (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18); and (2) Judas Iscariot (Matt. 10:4; Mark 3:19).

name: Kish
bio: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 23:21; 24:29).

name: Kore
bio: A Levite and temple-warder of the Korahites, the son of Asaph. He was father of Shallum and Meshelemiah, temple-porters (1 Chr. 9:19; 26:1).

name: Luke
bio: The evangelist, was a Gentile. The date and circumstances of his conversion are unknown. According to his own statement (Luke 1:2), he was not an “eye-witness and minister of the word from the beginning.” It is probable that he was a physician in Troas, and was there converted by…

name: Maaseiah
bio: The father of the priest Zephaniah (Jer. 21:1; 37:3).

name: Machir
bio: A descendant of the preceding, residing at Lo-debar, where he maintained Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth till he was taken under the care of David (2 Sam. 9:4), and where he afterwards gave shelter to David himself when he was a fugitive (17:27).

name: Malluch
bio: A priest who returned from Babylon (Neh. 12:2).

name: Mamre
bio: An Amoritish chief in alliance with Abraham (Gen. 14:13, 24).

name: Memucan
bio: Dignified, one of the royal counsellors at the court of Ahasuerus, by whose suggestion Vashti was divorced (Esther 1:14, 16, 21).

name: Michah
bio: The first in rank of the priests of the family of Kohathites (1 Chr. 23:20).

name: Mikloth
bio: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:32; 9:37, 38).

name: Miniamin
bio: A chief priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5), called Mijamin (10:7) and Miniamin (12:17).

name: Moadiah
bio: A priest (Neh. 10:8).

name: Mother of the Wife of Simon
Naamah
bio: The daughter of the king of Ammon, one of the wives of Solomon, the only one who appears to have borne him a son, viz., Rehoboam (1 Kings 14:21, 31).

name: Nahash
bio: King of the Ammonites in the time of Saul. The inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead having been exposed to great danger from Nahash, sent messengers to Gibeah to inform Saul of their extremity. He promptly responded to the call, and gathering together an army he marched against Nahash.

name: Nahath
bio: One of the four sons of Reuel, the son of Esau (Gen. 36:13, 17).

name: Nahath
bio: A Kohathite Levite (1 Chr. 6:26).

name: Obadiah
bio: A Levite, after the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:16).

name: Omar
bio: Eloquent, the son of Eliphaz, who was Esau’s eldest son (Gen. 36:11-15).

name: Pekahiah
bio: The Lord opened his eyes, the son and successor of Menahem on the throne of Israel. He was murdered in the royal palace of Samaria by Pekah, one of the captains of his army (2 Kings 15:23-26), after a reign of two years (B.C. 761-759).

name: Phichol
bio: Great, the chief captain of the army of Abimelech, the Philistine king of Gerar. He entered into an alliance with Abraham with reference to a certain well which, from this circumstance, was called Beersheba (q.v.), “the well of the oath” (Gen. 21:22, 32; 26:26).

name: Philip
bio: Mentioned only in connection with the imprisonment of John the Baptist (Matt. 14:3; Mark 6:17; Luke 3:19). He was the son of Herod the Great, and the first husband of Herodias, and the father of Salome. (See HEROD PHILIP I.)

name: Phut
bio: One of the sons of Ham (Gen. 10:6).

name: Rehabiah
bio: Enlargement of the Lord, the son of Eliezer, and grandson of Moses (1 Chr. 23:17; 24:21).

name: Rimmon
bio: A man of Beeroth (2 Sam. 4:2), one of the four Gibeonite cities. (See Josh. 9:17.)

name: Serah
bio: Abundance; princess, the daughter of Asher and grand-daughter of Jacob (Gen. 46:17); called also Sarah (Num. 26:46; R.V., “Serah”).

name: Shalmaneser
bio: An Assyrian king (Hos. 10:14), identified with Shalmaneser II. (Sayce) or IV. (Lenormant), the successor of Pul on the throne of Assyria (B.C. 728). He made war against Hoshea, the king of Israel, whom he subdued and compelled to pay an annual tribute.

name: Shammah
bio: One of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:13, 17).

name: Shammua
bio: One of David’s sons by Bathsheba (1 Chr. 3:5); called also Shammua (14:4).

name: Shebaniah
bio: Another Levite (Neh. 9:4, 5).

name: Shebaniah
bio: A priest who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3; marg., or Shebaniah).

name: Shemaiah
bio: The eldest son of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4-8).

name: Shemaiah
bio: A false prophet who opposed Jeremiah (Jer. 29:24-32).

name: Shemiramoth
bio: A Levite in David’s time (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

name: Shephatiah
bio: Ezra 2:4.

name: Shimron
bio: Watchman, the fourth son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13; 1 Chr. 7:1; R.V., correctly, “Shimron”).

name: Shobab
bio: One of David’s sons by Bathseheba (2 Sam. 5:14).

name: Shuah
bio: A Canaanite whose daughter was married to Judah (1 Chr. 2:3).

name: Shubael
bio: One of the descendants of Gershom, who had charge of the temple treasures in the time of David (1 Chr. 23:16; 26:24).

name: Simon
bio: A Jew of Cyrene, in North Africa, then a province of Libya. A hundred thousand Jews from Palestine had been settled in this province by Ptolemy Soter (B.C. 323-285), where by this time they had greatly increased in number.

name: Stephanas
bio: Crown, a member of the church at Corinth, whose family were among those the apostle had baptized (1 Cor. 1:16; 16:15, 17). He has been supposed by some to have been the “jailer of Philippi” (comp. Acts 16:33).

name: Talmai
bio: One of the Anakim of Hebron, who were slain by the men of Judah under Caleb (Num. 13:22; Josh. 15:14; Judg. 1:10).

name: Talmai
bio: A king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after he had put Amnon to death (2 Sam. 3:3; 13:37). His daughter, Maachah, was one of David’s wives, and the mother of Absalom (1 Chr. 3:2).

name: Trophimus
bio: A foster-child, an Ephesian who accompanied Paul during a part of his third missionary journey (Acts 20:4; 21:29).

name: Urijah
bio: The father of Meremoth, mentioned in Ezra 8:33.

name: Urijah
bio: A prophet of Kirjath-jearim in the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah (Jer. 26:20-23). He fled into Egypt from the cruelty of the king, but having been brought back he was beheaded and his body “cast into the graves of the common people.”

name: Zacchaeus
bio: Pure, a superintendant of customs; a chief tax-gather (publicanus) at Jericho (Luke 19:1-10). “The collection of customs at Jericho, which at this time produced and exported a considerable quantity of balsam, was undoubtedly an important post, and would account for Zacchaeus bein…

name: Zaccur
bio: A son of Asaph, and chief of one of the courses of singers as arranged by David (1 Chr. 25:2, 10).

name: Zachariah
bio: Son of Jeroboam II., king of Israel. On the death of his father there was an interregnum of ten years, at the end of which he succeeded to the throne, which he occupied only six months, having been put to death by Shallum, who usurped the throne.

name: Zacharias
bio: The son or grandson of Jehoiada, the high priest in the times of Ahaziah and Joash. After the death of Jehoiada he boldly condemned both the king and the people for their rebellion against God (2 Chr.

name: Zattu
bio: Id., one whose descendants returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:8; Neh. 7:13); probably the same as Zatthu.

name: Zeeb
bio: The wolf, one of the two leaders of the great Midianite host which invaded Israel and was utterly routed by Gideon.

name: Zeresh
bio: Star of Venus, the wife of Haman, whom she instigated to prepare a gallows for Mordecai (Esther 5:10).

name: Zillah
bio: Shadow, one of the wives of Lamech, of the line of Cain, and mother of Tubal-cain (Gen. 4:19, 22).

name: Zipporah
bio: A female bird. Reuel’s daughter, who became the wife of Moses (Ex. 2:21). In consequence of the event recorded in Ex.

name: Zuph
bio: Honeycomb, a Kohathite Levite, ancestor of Elkanah and Samuel (1 Sam. 1:1); called also Zophai (1 Chr. 6:26).

name: Abdon
bio: The son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, the tenth judge of Israel (Judg. 12:13-15). He is probably the Bedan of 1 Sam. 12:11.

name: Abdon
bio: The first-born of Gibeon of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:30; 9:36).

name: Abiah
bio: The second son of Samuel (1 Sam. 8:2; 1 Chr. 6:28). His conduct, along with that of his brother, as a judge in Beer-sheba, to which office his father had appointed him, led to popular discontent, and ultimately provoked the people to demand a royal form of government.

name: Abida
bio: Or Abi’dah, father of knowledge; knowing, one of the five sons of Midian, who was the son of Abraham by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:33), and apparently the chief of an Arab tribe.

name: Abihail
bio: The father of Esther and uncle of Mordecai (Esther 2:15).

name: Abijah
bio: The daughter of Zechariah (2 Chr. 29:1; comp. Isa. 8:2), and afterwards the wife of Ahaz. She is also called Abi (2 Kings 18:2).

name: Abijah
bio: A descendant of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, a chief of one of the twenty-four orders into which the priesthood was divided by David (1 Chr. 24:10). The order of Abijah was one of those which did not return from the Captivity (Ezra 2:36-39; Neh. 7:39-42; 12:1).

name: Abimael
bio: Father of Mael, one of the sons or descendants of Joktan, in Northern Arabia (Gen. 10:28; 1 Chr. 1:22).

name: Abishur
bio: Father of the wall; i.e., “mason”, one of the two sons of Shammai of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:28, 29).

name: Abital
bio: Father of dew; i.e., “fresh”, David’s fifth wife (2 Sam. 3:4).

name: Adaiah
bio: Timely (1 Chr. 6:21). A Gershonite Levite.

name: Adbeel
bio: Miracle of God, the third of the twelve sons of Ishmael, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:13; 1 Chr. 1:29).

name: Adrammelech
bio: A son of Sennacherib, king of Assyria (2 Kings 19:37; Isa. 37:38).

name: Adriel
bio: Flock of God, the son of Barzillai, the Meholathite, to whom Saul gave in marriage his daughter Merab (1 Sam. 18:19). The five sons that sprang from this union were put to death by the Gibeonites (2 Sam. 21:8, 9.

name: Agabus
bio: A “prophet,” probably one of the seventy disciples of Christ. He prophesied at Antioch of an approaching famine (Acts 11:27, 28).

name: Ahab
bio: A false prophet referred to by Jeremiah (Jer. 29:21), of whom nothing further is known.

name: Ahiam
bio: Mother’s brother, one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:33; 1 Chr. 11:35).

name: Ahio
bio: One of the sons of Jehiel the Gibeonite (1 Chr. 8:31; 9:37).

name: Akan
bio: He twists, one of the sons of Ezer, the son of Seir the Horite (1 Chr. 1:42).

name: Alemeth
bio: One of the sons of Jehoadah, or Jarah, son of Ahaz (1 Chr. 8:36).

name: Alexander
bio: A coppersmith who, with Hymenaeus and others, promulgated certain heresies regarding the resurrection (1 Tim. 1:19; 2 Tim. 4:14), and made shipwreck of faith and of a good conscience. Paul excommunicated him (1 Tim. 1:20; comp. 1 Cor. 5:5).

name: Allon
bio: The son of Jedaiah, of the family of the Simeonites, who expelled the Hamites from the valley of Gedor (1 Chr. 4:37).

name: Almodad
bio: Immeasurable, the first named of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:26), the founder of an Arabian tribe.

name: Amariah
bio: One of the descendants of Aaron by Eleazar (1 Chr. 6:7, 52). He was probably the last of the high priests of Eleazar’s line prior to the transfer of that office to Eli, of the line of Ithamar.

name: Amariah
bio: A Levite, son of Hebron, of the lineage of Moses (1 Chr. 23:19; 24:23).

name: Amasai
bio: A Levite, son of Elkanah, of the ancestry of Samuel (1 Chr. 6:25, 35).

name: Amittai
bio: True, the father of Jonah the prophet, a native of Gath-hepher (2 Kings 14:25; Jonah 1:1).

name: Amminadab
bio: Chief of the 112 descendants of Uzziel the Levite (1 Chr. 15:10, 11).

name: Amon
bio: The governor of Samaria in the time of Ahab. The prophet Micaiah was committed to his custody (1 Kings 22:26; 2 Chr. 18:25).

name: Amraphel
bio: King of Shinar, southern Chaldea, one of the confederates of Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, in a war against Sodom and cities of the plain (Gen. 14:1, 4). It is now found that Amraphel (or Ammirapaltu) is the Khammu-rabi whose name appears on recently-discovered monuments.

name: Anamim
bio: The name of an Egyptian tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11).

name: Ananias (High Priest)
bio: The high priest before whom Paul was brought in the procuratorship of Felix (Acts 23:2, 5, 24). He was so enraged at Paul’s noble declaration, “I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day,” that he commanded one of his attendants to smite him on the mouth.

name: Anath
bio: An answer; i.e., to “prayer”, the father of Shamgar, who was one of the judges of Israel (Judg. 3:31).

name: Aner
bio: A Canaanitish chief who joined his forces with those of Abraham in pursuit of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:13, 24).

name: Aran
bio: Wild goat, a descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:28).

name: Archippus
bio: Master of the horse, a “fellow-soldier” of Paul’s (Philemon 1:2), whom he exhorts to renewed activity (Col. 4:17). He was a member of Philemon’s family, probably his son.

name: Arioch (king of Ellasar)
bio: A king of Ellasar who was confederate with Chedorlamer (Gen. 14:1, 9). The tablets recently discovered by Mr. Pinches (see CHALDEA) show the true reading is Eri-Aku of Larsa.

name: Arkite
bio: (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15), a designation of certain descendants from the Phoenicians or Sidonians, the inhabitants of Arka, 12 miles north of Tripoli, opposite the northern extremity of Lebanon.

name: Ater
bio: Ezra 2:16.

name: Ater
bio: Ezra 2:42.

name: Azareel
bio: A priest (1 Chr. 9:12).

name: Azariah
bio: High priest in the reign of Uzziah, king of Judah (2 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 26:17-20). He was contemporary with the prophets Isaiah, Amos, and Joel.

name: Azmaveth
bio: One of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:31).

name: Azubah
bio: The daughter of Shilhi, and mother of king Jehoshaphat (1 Kings 22:42).

name: Azubah
bio: The wife of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:18, 19).

name: Baal
bio: A Benjamite, son of Jehiel, the progenitor of the Gibeonites (1 Chr. 8:30; 9:36).

name: Baanah
bio: The father of Heled, who was one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:29; 1 Chr. 11:30).

name: Baladan
bio: He has given a son, the father of the Babylonian king (2 Kings 20:12; Isa. 39:1) Merodach-baladan (q.v.).

name: Barachel
bio: Whom God has blessed, a Buzite, the father of Elihu, one of Job’s friends (Job 32:2, 6).

name: Barkos
bio: Painter, (Ezra 2:53; Neh. 7:55). The father of some of the Nethinim.

name: Barzillai
bio: A priest who married a daughter of the preceding (Ezra 2:61).

name: Ben-ammi
bio: Son of my kindred; i.e., “born of incest”, the son of Lot by his youngest daughter (Gen. 19:38).

name: Beor
bio: The father of Bela, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:32).

name: Beriah
bio: A Benjamite who with his brother Shema founded Ajalon and expelled the Gittites (1 Chr. 8:13).

name: Bigthana
bio: One of the eunuchs who “kept the door” in the court of Ahasuerus. With Teresh he conspired against the king’s life. Mordecai detected the conspiracy, and the culprits were hanged (Esther 2:21-23; 6:1-3).

name: Bilshan
bio: Son of the tongue; i.e., “eloquent”, a man of some note who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:2; Neh. 7:7).

name: Casluhim
bio: Fortified, a people descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:14; 1 Chr. 1:12). Their original seat was probably somewhere in Lower Egypt, along the sea-coast to the south border of Palestine.

name: Chenaniah
bio: Whom Jehovah hath made. “Chief of the Levites,” probably a Kohathite (1 Chr. 15:22), and therefore not the same as mentioned in 26:29.

name: Chushan-rishathaim
bio: Cush of double wickedness, or governor of two presidencies, the king of Mesopotamia who oppressed Israel in the generation immediately following Joshua (Judg. 3:8).

name: Claudius (4th Roman Emperor)
bio: The fourth Roman emperor. He succeeded Caligula (A.D. 41). Though in general he treated the Jews, especially those in Asia and Egypt, with great indulgence, yet about the middle of his reign (A.D. 49) he banished them all from Rome (Acts 18:2).

name: Cleophas
bio: (abbreviation of Cleopatros), one of the two disciples with whom Jesus conversed on the way to Emmaus on the day of the resurrection (Luke 24:18). We know nothing definitely regarding him. It is not certain that he was the Clopas of John 19:25, or the Alphaeus of Matt.

name: Crispus
bio: Curled, the chief of the synagogue at Corinth (Acts 18:8). He was converted and, with his family, baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14).

name: Daniel
bio: David’s second son, “born unto him in Hebron, of Abigail the Carmelitess” (1 Chr. 3:1). He is called also Chileab (2 Sam. 3:3).

name: Dedan (son of Raamah)
bio: A son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7). His descendants are mentioned in Isa. 21:13, and Ezek. 27:15. They probably settled among the sons of Cush, on the north-west coast of the Persian Gulf.

name: Dedan (son of Jokshan)
bio: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom. They probably led a pastoral life.

name: Delaiah
bio: The head of one of the bands of exiles that returned under Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:60; Neh. 7:62).

name: Delaiah
bio: A son of Shemaiah, and one of the courtiers to whom Jeremiah’s first roll of prophecy was read (Jer. 36:12).

name: Dodanim
bio: Leaders, a race descended from Javan (Gen. 10:4). They are known in profane history as the Dardani, originally inhabiting Illyricum. They were a semi-Pelasgic race, and in the ethnographical table (Gen. 10) they are grouped with the Chittim (q.v.). In 1 Chr.

name: Dodo
bio: A Bethlehemite, and father of Elhanan, who was one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:24).

name: Ebal (son of Shobal)
bio: A descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:23).

name: Ebal (son of Joktan)
bio: A descendant of Eber (1 Chr. 1:22), called also Obal (Gen. 10:28).

name: Eder
bio: The second of the three sons of Mushi, of the family of Merari, appointed to the Levitical office (1 Chr. 23:23; 24:30).

name: Eglah
bio: A heifer, one of David’s wives, and mother of Ithream (2 Sam. 3:5; 1 Chr. 3:3). According to a Jewish tradition she was Michal.

name: Elah
bio: One of the Edomite chiefs or “dukes” of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:41).

name: Elam (son of Shem)
bio: Highland, the son of Shem (Gen. 10:22), and the name of the country inhabited by his descendants (14:1, 9; Isa. 11:11; 21:2, etc.) lying to the east of Babylonia, and extending to the shore of the Mediterranean, a distance in a direct line of about 1,000 miles.

name: Eldad
bio: Whom God has loved, one of the seventy elders whom Moses appointed (Num. 11:26, 27) to administer justice among the people. He, with Medad, prophesied in the camp instead of going with the rest to the tabernacle, as Moses had commanded.

name: Eleasah
bio: One of the descendants of Judah, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:39, “Eleasah”).

name: Eleazar
bio: The son of Dodo the Ahohite, of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the three most eminent of David’s thirty-seven heroes (1 Chr. 11:12) who broke through the Philistine host and brought him water from the well of Bethlehem (2 Sam. 23:9, 16).

name: Elhanan
bio: A warrior of the time of David famed for his exploits. In the Authorized Version (2 Sam. 21:19) it is recorded that “Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim, a Bethlehemite, slew the brother of Goliath.” The Revised Version here rightly omits the words “the brother of.” They were introdu…

name: Elhanan
bio: The son of Dodo, and one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:24).

name: Eliam
bio: The father of Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah (2 Sam. 11:3). In 1 Chr. 3:5 his name is Ammiel.

name: Eliathah
bio: To whom God will come, one of the foureen sons of the Levite Heman, and musician of the temple in the time of David (1 Chr. 25:4).

name: Elipheleh
bio: God will distinguish him, one of the porters appointed to play “on the Sheminith” on the occasion of the bringing up of the ark to the city of David (1 Chr. 15:18, 21).

name: Elishah
bio: The oldest of the four sons of Javan (Gen. 10:4), whose descendants peopled Greece. It has been supposed that Elishah’s descendants peopled the Peloponnesus, which was known by the name of Elis. This may be meant by “the isles of Elishah” (Ezek. 27:7).

name: Elishama
bio: One of David’s sons (2 Sam. 5:16).

name: Elkanah
bio: The second son of Korah (Ex. 6:24), or, according to 1 Chr. 6:22, 23, more correctly his grandson.

name: Elon
bio: A Hittite, father of Bashemath, Esau’s wife (Gen. 26:34).

name: Elon
bio: One of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

name: Elon
bio: The eleventh of the Hebrew judges. He held office for ten years (Judg. 12:11, 12). He is called the Zebulonite.

name: Elymas
bio: Magician or sorcerer, the Arabic name of the Jew Bar-jesus, who withstood Paul and Barnabas in Cyprus. He was miraculously struck with blindness (Acts 13:11).

name: Enoch (son of Cain)
bio: The eldest son of Cain (Gen. 4:17), who built a city east of Eden in the land of Nod, and called it “after the name of his son Enoch.” This is the first “city” mentioned in Scripture.

name: Epher
bio: One of the sons of Midian, who was Abraham’s son by Keturah (Gen. 25:4).

name: Eshcol
bio: A young Amoritish chief who joined Abraham in the recovery of Lot from the hands of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:13, 24).

name: Ethan
bio: A Levite of the family of Gershom (1 Chr. 6:21), probably the same as Ethan (42).

name: Evil-merodach
bio: Merodach’s man, the son and successor of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon (2 Kings 25:27; Jer. 52:31, 34). He seems to have reigned but two years (B.C. 562-560).

name: Ezekiel
bio: One of the great prophets, the son of Buzi the priest (Ezek. 1:3). He was one of the Jewish exiles who settled at Tel-Abib, on the banks of the Chebar, “in the land of the Chaldeans.” He was probably carried away captive with Jehoiachin (1:2; 2 Kings 24:14-16) about B.C. 597.

name: Gahar
bio: Lurking-place, one of the chief of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:47).

name: Gaius
bio: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14).

name: Gamaliel
bio: The son of rabbi Simeon, and grandson of the famous rabbi Hillel. He was a Pharisse, and therefore the opponent of the party of the Sadducees.

name: Gedaliah
bio: the son of Jeduthum (1 Chr. 25:3, 9).

name: Girgasite
bio: Dwelling in clayey soil, the descendants of the fifth son of Canaan (Gen. 10:16), one of the original tribes inhabiting the land of Canaan before the time of the Israelites (Gen. 15:21; Deut. 7:1). They were a branch of the great family of the Hivites.

name: Hadar
bio: A son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15); in 1 Chr. 1:30 written Hadad.

name: Hadoram
bio: The fifth son of Joktan, the founder of an Arab tribe (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21).

name: Hammelech
bio: The king’s, the father of Jerahmeel, mentioned in Jer. 36:26. Some take this word as a common noun, “the king”, and understand that Jerahmeel was Jehoiakim’s son. Probably, however, it is to be taken as a proper name.

name: Hanan
bio: A descendant of Saul (1 Chr. 8:38).

name: Hanan
bio: One of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:46).

name: Hanan
bio: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra (Neh. 8:7).

name: Hanani
bio: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4, 25).

name: Hanani
bio: Probably a brother of Nehemiah (Neh. 1:2; 7:2), who reported to him the melancholy condition of Jerusalem. Nehemiah afterwards appointed him to have charge of the city gates.

name: Hananiah
bio: Son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:19, 21).

name: Hananiah
bio: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4, 23).

name: Harhur
bio: Fever, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:51).

name: Harsha
bio: Worker or enchanter, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:52; Neh. 7:54).

name: Hasrah
bio: Poverty, “keeper of the wardrobe,” i.e., of the sacerdotal vestments (2 Chr. 34:22); called Harhas 2 Kings 22:14. He was husband of the prophetess Huldah.

name: Hasshub
bio: A Levite of the family of Merari (Neh. 11:15; 1 Chr. 9:14).

name: Hasupha
bio: Uncovered, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:43; Neh. 7:46).

name: Hatipha
bio: Captured, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:54).

name: Hatita
bio: Exploration, one of the temple porters or janitors (Ezra 2:42). He returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel.

name: Hattush
bio: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:2).

name: Havilah (son of Cush)
bio: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

name: Havilah (son of Joktan)
bio: A son of Joktan (Gen. 10:29; 1 Chr. 1:23).

name: Hazarmaveth
bio: Court of death, the third son of Joktan, and a region in Arabia-Felix settled by him (Gen. 10:26; 1 Chr. 1:20). It is probably the modern province of Hadramaut, situated on the Indian Ocean east of the modern Yemen.

name: Helah
bio: Rust, (1 Chr. 4:5, 7), one of the wives of Ashur.

name: Helek
bio: A portion, (Josh. 17:2), descended from Manasseh.

name: Helem
bio: Zech. 6:10, one who returned from Babylon.

name: Henadad
bio: Favour of Hadad, the name of a Levite after the Captivity (Ezra 3:9).

name: Hezrai
bio: A Carmelite, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:37).

name: Hillel
bio: Praising, a Pirathonite, father of the judge Abdon (Judg. 12:13, 15).

name: Hobab
bio: Beloved, the Kenite, has been usually identified with Jethro (q.v.), Ex. 18:5, 27; comp. Num. 10:29, 30. In Judg. 4:11, the word rendered “father-in-law” means properly any male relative by marriage (comp. Gen.

name: Hotham
bio: A stroke, great-grandson of Asher (1 Chr. 7:35).

name: Hul
bio: Circle, the second son of Aram (Gen. 10:23), and grandson of Shem.

name: Huldah
bio: Weasel, a prophetess; the wife of Shallum. She was consulted regarding the “book of the law” discovered by the high priest Hilkiah (2 Kings 22:14-20; 2 Chr. 34:22-28).

name: Hur
bio: One of the five princes of Midian who were defeated and slain by the Israelites under the command of Phinehas (Num. 31:8).

name: Hurai
bio: Linen-worker, one of David’s heroes, a native of the valley of Mount Gaash (1 Chr. 11:32).

name: Ibzan
bio: Illustrious, the tenth judge of Israel (Judg. 12:8-10). He ruled seven years.

name: Ilai
bio: An Ahohite, one of David’s chief warriors (1 Chr. 11:29); called also Zalmon (2 Sam. 23:28).

name: Ira
bio: An Ithrite, also one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:38).

name: Iram
bio: Citizen, chief of an Edomite tribe in Mount Seir (Gen. 36:43).

name: Ishbak
bio: Leaving, one of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

name: Ittai
bio: A Benjamite, one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:29).

name: Jaala
bio: A wild she-goat, one of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned from the Captivity (Neh. 7:58).

name: Jaaziah
bio: Comforted by Jehovah, a descendant of Merari the Levite (1 Chr. 24:26, 27).

name: Jaaziel
bio: Comforted by God, a Levitical musician (1 Chr. 15:18).

name: Jabez
bio: A descendant of Judah, of whom it is recorded that “God granted him that which he requested” (1 Chr. 4:9, 10).

name: Jachin
bio: One of the priests who returned from the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

name: Jaddua
bio: The last high priest mentioned in the Old Testament (Neh. 12:11, 22), sons of Jonathan.

name: Jahath
bio: A son of Shimei, and grandson of Gershom (1 Chr. 23:10).

name: Jahaziel
bio: The third son of Hebron (1 Chr. 23:19).

name: Jair
bio: The father of Elhanan, who slew Lahmi, the brother of Goliath (1 Chr. 20:5).

name: Jairus
bio: A ruler of the synagogue at Capernaum, whose only daughter Jesus restored to life (Mark 5:22; Luke 8:41). Entering into the chamber of death, accompanied by Peter and James and John and the father and mother of the maiden, he went forward to the bed whereon the corpse lay, and sa…

name: Jasher
bio: Upright. “The Book of Jasher,” rendered in the LXX. “the Book of the Upright One,” by the Vulgate “the Book of Just Ones,” was probably a kind of national sacred song-book, a collection of songs in praise of the heroes of Israel, a “book of golden deeds,” a national anthology.

name: Jashobeam
bio: Dweller among the people; or to whom the people turn, the Hachmonite (1 Chr. 11:11), one of David’s chief heroes who joined him at Ziklag (12:6).

name: Jebusite
bio: The name of the original inhabitants of Jebus, mentioned frequently among the seven nations doomed to destruction (Gen. 10:16; 15:21; Ex. 3:8, 17; 13:5, etc.). At the time of the arrival of the Israelites in Palestine they were ruled by Adonizedek (Josh. 10:1, 23).

name: Jecoliah
bio: Able through Jehovah, the wife of King Amaziah, and mother of King Uzziah (2 Chr. 26:3).

name: Jehoaddan
bio: Jehovah his ornament, the wife of King Jehoash, and mother of King Amaziah (2 Kings 14:2).

name: Jehoshabeath
bio: Jehovah-swearing, the daughter of Jehoram, the king of Israel. She is called Jehoshabeath in 2 Chr. 22:11. She was the only princess of the royal house who was married to a high priest, Jehoiada (2 Chr. 22:11).

name: Jehoshaphat
bio: The son of Nimshi, and father of Jehu, king of Israel (2 Kings 9:2, 14).

name: Jehozabad
bio: The son of Shomer, one of the two conspirators who put king Jehoash to death in Millo in Jerusalem (2 Kings 12:21).

name: Jeremoth
bio: 1 Chr. 24:30, a Merarite Levite.

name: Jerimoth
bio: A Levitical musician under Heman his father (1 Chr. 25:4).

name: Jeroham
bio: 1 Chr. 9:12; a priest, perhaps the same as in Neh. 11:12.

name: Jerushah
bio: Possession, or possessed; i.e., “by a husband”, the wife of Uzziah, and mother of king Jotham (2 Kings 15:33).

name: Jeshaiah
bio: A Kohathite Levite, the father of Joram, of the family of Eliezer (1 Chr. 26:25); called also Isshiah (24:21).

name: Jeshaiah
bio: One of the sons of Jeduthum (1 Chr. 25:3, 15).

name: Jesharelah
bio: Upright towards God, the head of the seventh division of Levitical musicians (1 Chr. 25:14).

name: Jeshua
bio: Ezra 2:6; Neh. 7:11.

name: Jetheth
bio: A peg, or a prince, one of the Edomitish kings of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:40).

name: Jetur
bio: An enclosure, one of the twelve sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

name: Jeush
bio: A Levite, one of the sons of Shimei (1 Chr. 23:10, 11).

name: Joab
bio: Ezra 2:6.

name: Joanna
bio: The wife of Chuza, the steward of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee (Luke 8:3). She was one of the women who ministered to our Lord, and to whom he appeared after his resurrection (Luke 8:3; 24:10).

name: Joash
bio: One of King Ahab’s sons (1 Kings 22:26).

name: Jobab (son of Joktan)
bio: One of the sons of Joktan, and founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 10:29).

name: Jochebed
bio: Jehovah is her glory, the wife of Amram, and the mother of Miriam, Aaron, and Moses (Num. 26:59). She is spoken of as the sister of Kohath, Amram’s father (Ex. 6:20; comp. 16, 18; 2:1-10).

name: Joel
bio: A Levite of the family of Gershom (1 Chr. 15:7, 11).

name: Joel
bio: The second of the twelve minor prophets. He was the son of Pethuel. His personal history is only known from his book.

name: Joram
bio: The son of Tou, king of Hamath, sent by his father to congratulate David on his victory over Hadarezer, king of Syria (1 Chr. 18:10; called Joram 2 Sam. 8:10).

name: Joseph (son of Asaph)
bio: One of the sons of Asaph, head of the first division of sacred musicians (1 Chr. 25:2, 9).

name: Jucal
bio: Able, the son of Shelemiah. He is also called Jucal (Jer. 38:1). He was one of the two persons whom Zedekiah sent to request the prophet Jeremiah to pray for the kingdom (Jer. 37:3) during the time of its final siege by Nebuchadnezzar. He was accompanied by Zephaniah (q.v.).

name: Julius
bio: The centurion of the Augustan cohort, or the emperor’s body-guard, in whose charge Paul was sent prisoner to Rome (Acts 27:1, 3, 43). He entreated Paul “courteously,” showing in many ways a friendly regard for him.

name: Kedemah
bio: Eastward, the last-named of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

name: Kelita
bio: Dwarf, a Levite who assisted Ezra in expounding the law to the people (Neh. 8:7; 10:10).

name: Laish
bio: The father of Phalti (1 Sam. 25:44).

name: Lemuel
bio: Dedicated to God, a king whom his mother instructed (Prov. 31:1-9). Nothing is certainly known concerning him. The rabbis identified him with Solomon.

name: Lo-ruhamah
bio: Not pitied, the name of the prophet Hosea’s first daughter, a type of Jehovah’s temporary rejection of his people (Hos. 1:6; 2:23).

name: Lucius
bio: Of Cyrene, a Christian teacher at Antioch (Acts 13:1), and Paul’s kinsman (Rom. 16:21). His name is Latin, but his birthplace seems to indicate that he was one of the Jews of Cyrene, in North Africa.

name: Lud
bio: The fourth son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17), ancestor of the Lydians probably.

name: Ludim
bio: Probably the same as Lud (2) (comp. Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11). They are associated (Jer. 46:9) with African nations as mercenaries of the king of Egypt.

name: Maacah
bio: A daughter of Talmai, king of the old native population of Geshur. She became one of David’s wives, and was the mother of Absalom (2 Sam. 3:3).

name: Maachah
bio: The father of Achish, the king of Gath (1 Kings 2:39), called also Maoch (1 Sam. 27:2).

name: Maaseiah
bio: One of the Levites whom David appointed as porter for the ark (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

name: Maasiai
bio: Work of Jehovah, one of the priests resident at Jerusalem at the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:12).

name: Madai
bio: Middle land, the third “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the name by which the Medes are known on the Assyrian monuments.

name: Mahath
bio: A Kohathite Levite, father of Elkanah (1 Chr. 6:35).

name: Mahazioth
bio: Visions, a Kohathite Levite, chief of the twenty-third course of musicians (1 Chr. 25:4, 30).

name: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
bio: Plunder speedeth; spoil hasteth, (Isa. 8:1-3; comp. Zeph. 1:14), a name Isaiah was commanded first to write in large characters on a tablet, and afterwards to give as a symbolical name to a son that was to be born to him (Isa.

name: Malcham
bio: (2 Sam. 12:30, Heb., R.V., “their king;” Jer. 49:1, 3, R.V.; Zeph. 1:5), the national idol of the Ammonites. When Rabbah was taken by David, the crown of this idol was among the spoils. The weight is said to have been “a talent of gold” (above 100 lbs.).

name: Mallothi
bio: My fulness, a Kohathite Levite, one of the sons of Heman the Levite (1 Chr. 25:4), and chief of the nineteenth division of the temple musicians (26).

name: Mash
bio: (= Meshech 1 Chr. 1:17), one of the four sons of Aram, and the name of a tribe descended from him (Gen. 10:23) inhabiting some part probably of Mesopotamia.

name: Massa
bio: A lifting up, gift, one of the sons of Ishmael, the founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:14); a nomad tribe inhabiting the Arabian desert toward Babylonia.

name: Mattan
bio: A priest of Baal, slain before his altar during the reformation under Jehoiada (2 Kings 11:18).

name: Mattaniah
bio: A Levite, son of Heman, the chief of the ninth class of temple singers (1 Chr. 25:4, 16).

name: Matthias
bio: Gift of God. Acts 1:23.

name: Medan
bio: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom. They probably led a pastoral life.

name: Mehetabel
bio: Wife of Hadad, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:39).

name: Mehunim
bio: Habitations, (2 Chr. 26:7; R.V. “Meunim,” Vulg. Ammonitae), a people against whom Uzziah waged a successful war. This word is in Hebrew the plural of Ma’on, and thus denotes the Maonites who inhabited the country on the eastern side of the Wady el-Arabah.

name: Melech
bio: King, the second of Micah’s four sons (1 Chr. 8:35), and thus grandson of Mephibosheth.

name: Melzar
bio: Probably a Persian word meaning master of wine, i.e., chief butler; the title of an officer at the Babylonian court (Dan. 1:11, 16) who had charge of the diet of the Hebrew youths.

name: Mered
bio: Rebellion, one of the sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

name: Meshillemith
bio: A priest, the son of Immer (Neh. 11:13).

name: Meshullam
bio: A priest (1 Chr. 9:12).

name: Mezahab
bio: Water of gold, the father of Matred (Gen. 36:39; 1 Chr. 1:50), and grandfather of Mehetabel, wife of Hadar, the last king of Edom.

name: Mibsam
bio: One of Ishmael’s twelve sons, and head of an Arab tribe (Gen. 25:13).

name: Mibzar
bio: Fortress, one of the Edomitish “dukes” descended from Esau (Gen. 36:42; 1 Chr. 1:53).

name: Micah
bio: “The Morasthite,” so called to distinguish him from Micaiah, the son of Imlah (1 Kings 22:8). He was a prophet of Judah, a contemporary of Isaiah (Micah 1:1), a native of Moresheth of Gath (1:14, 15). Very little is known of the circumstances of his life (comp. Jer. 26:18, 19).

name: Micha
bio: The son of Zabdi, a Levite of the family of Asaph (Neh. 11:17, 22).

name: Michaiah
bio: A Levite (Neh. 12:35).

name: Michaiah
bio: 2 Kings 22:12.

name: Michaiah
bio: The son of Gemariah. He reported to the king’s officers Jeremiah’s prediction, which he had heard Baruch read (Jer. 36:11, 13) from his father Gemariah’s chamber in the temple.

name: Mishael
bio: A Levite; the eldest of the three sons of Uzziel (Ex. 6:22).

name: Mishma
bio: One of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:14), and founder of an Arab tribe.

name: Mishma
bio: A Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:25, 26).

name: Mispereth
bio: Number, one of the Jews who accompanied Zerubbabel from Babylon (Ezra 2:2); called also Mispereth (Neh. 7:7).

name: Naarah
bio: A girl, the second of Ashur’s two wives, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:5, 6).

name: Nadab
bio: One of the sons of Shammai in the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:28, 30).

name: Naharai
bio: Snorer, a Berothite, one of David’s heroes, and armour-bearer of Joab (1 Chr. 11:39).

name: Naphtuhim
bio: A Hamitic tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13). Others identify this word with Napata, the name of the city and territory on the southern frontier of Mizraim, the modern Meroe, at the great bend of the Nile at Soudan.

name: Nehemiah
bio: Ezra 2:2; Neh. 7:7.

name: Nergal-sharezer
bio: Another of the “princes,” who bore the title of “Rabmag.” He was one of those who were sent to release Jeremiah from prison (Jer. 39:13) by “the captain of the guard.” He was a Babylonian grandee of high rank.

name: Neziah
bio: Victory; pure, Ezra 2:54; Neh. 7:56.

name: Nogah
bio: Splendour, one of David’s sons, born at Jerusalem (1 Chr. 3:7).

name: Obadiah
bio: A descendant of Saul (1 Chr. 8:38).

name: Ohad
