bio: United, or power, the third son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10).

name: Onesimus
bio: Useful, a slave who, after robbing his master Philemon (q.v.) at Colosse, fled to Rome, where he was converted by the apostle Paul, who sent him back to his master with the epistle which bears his name.

name: Onesiphorus
bio: Bringing profit, an Ephesian Christian who showed great kindness to Paul at Rome. He served him in many things, and had oft refreshed him. Paul expresses a warm interest in him and his household (2 Tim. 1:16-18; 4:19).

name: Ophir
bio: One of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:29).

name: Orpah
bio: Forelock or fawn, a Moabitess, the wife of Chilion (Ruth 1:4; 4:10). On the death of her husband she accompanied Naomi, her mother-in-law, part of the way to Bethlehem, and then returned to Moab.

name: Ozni
bio: Hearing, one of the sons of Gad; also called Ezbon (Gen. 46:16; Num. 26:16).

name: Pedaiah
bio: The father of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:17-19).

name: Pelaiah
bio: A Levite who expounded the law (Neh. 8:7).

name: Pelatiah
bio: One of the twenty-five princes of the people against whom Ezekiel prophesied on account of their wicked counsel (Ezek. 11:1-13).

name: Perida
bio: One whose descendants returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:55); called also Perida (Neh. 7:57).

name: Phaltiel
bio: Deliverance of the Lord, the son of Laish of Gallim (1 Sam. 25:44)= Phaltiel (2 Sam. 3:15). Michal, David’s wife, was given to him.

name: Potiphar
bio: Dedicated to Ra; i.e., to the sun-god, the Egyptian to whom the Ishmaelites sold Joseph (Gen. 39:1). He was “captain of the guard”, i.e., chief, probably, of the state police, who, while they formed part of the Egyptian army, were also largely employed in civil duties (37:36;

name: Publius
bio: “the chief man of the island” of Malta (Acts 28:7), who courteously entertained Paul and his shipwrecked companions for three days, till they found a more permanent place of residence; for they remained on the island for three months, till the stormy season had passed.

name: Raamah
bio: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

name: Ram
bio: One of the sons of Jerahmeel (1 Chr. 2:25, 27).

name: Rapha
bio: A Benjamite, the son of Binea (1 Chr. 8:2, 37), a descendant of Saul.

name: Reba
bio: Fourth, one of the Midianite chiefs slain by the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 31:8; Josh. 13:21).

name: Reelaiah
bio: Thunder of the Lord, one of the princes who returned from the Exile (Neh. 7:7); called also Reelaiah (Ezra 2:2).

name: Rehob
bio: The father of Hadadezer, king of Tobah (2 Sam. 8:3, 12).

name: Rekem
bio: One of the five Midianite kings whom the Israelites destroyed (Num. 31:8).

name: Rekem
bio: One of the sons of Hebron (1 Chr. 2:43, 44).

name: Riphath
bio: A crusher, Gomer’s second son (Gen. 10:3), supposed to have been the ancestor of the Paphlagonians.

name: Romamti-ezer
bio: Elevation of help, one of the sons of Heman, “the king’s seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn.” He was head of the “four-and-twentieth” course of singers (1 Chr. 25:4, 31).

name: Sabtah
bio: Rest, the third son of Cush (Gen. 10:7; 1 Chr. 1:9).

name: Sabtecha
bio: The fifth son of Cush.

name: Sallu
bio: A priest (Neh. 12:7).

name: Salome
bio: The wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John (Mat. 27:56), and probably the sister of Mary, the mother of our Lord (John 19:25). She sought for her sons places of honour in Christ’s kingdom (Matt. 20:20, 21; comp. 19:28).

name: Seba
bio: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

name: Segub
bio: A descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 2:21, 22).

name: Seraiah
bio: The father of Joab (1 Chr. 4:13, 14).

name: Seraiah
bio: The son of Neriah. When Zedekiah made a journey to Babylon to do homage to Nebuchadnezzar, Seraiah had charge of the royal gifts to be presented on that occasion.

name: Sered
bio: Fear, one of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

name: Shallum
bio: Keeper of the temple vestments in the reign of Josiah (2 Kings 22:14).

name: Shallum
bio: One of the posterity of Judah (1 Chr. 2:40, 41).

name: Shamer
bio: A man of Asher (1 Chr. 7:32); called also Shamer (34).

name: Shamgar
bio: The Philistines from the maritime plain had made incursions into the Hebrew upland for the purposes of plunder, when one of this name, the son of Anath, otherwise unknown, headed a rising for the purpose of freeing the land from this oppression.

name: Shammah
bio: One of David’s mighties (2 Sam. 23:25); called also Shammoth (1 Chr. 11:27) and Shamhuth (27:8).

name: Sharar
bio: One of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:35); called also Sharar (2 Sam. 23:33).

name: Sharezer
bio: (god) protect the king!, a son of Sennacherib, king of Assyria. He and his brother Adrammelech murdered their father, and then fled into the land of Armenia (2 Kings 19:37).

name: Sheba (son of Raamah)
bio: Heb. shebha, the son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7), whose descendants settled with those of Dedan on the Persian Gulf.

name: Sheba (son of Joktan)
bio: Heb. id. A son of Joktan (Gen. 10:28), probably the founder of the Sabeans.

name: Sheba
bio: Heb. id. A son of Jokshan, who was a son of Abraham by Keturah (Gen. 25:3).

name: Shechaniah
bio: A priest whose sons are mentioned in 1 Chr. 3:21, 22.

name: Shechaniah
bio: The father of Shemaiah, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:29).

name: Shechem
bio: A descendant of Manasseh (Num. 26:31; Josh. 17:2).

name: Shelemiah
bio: Father of one of those who accused Jeremiah to Zedekiah (Jer. 37:3; 38:1).

name: Shemaiah
bio: A Levite (1 Chr. 9:16).

name: Shemaiah
bio: A Levite in the time of David, who with 200 of his brethren took part in the bringing up of the ark from Obed-edom to Hebron (1 Chr. 15:8).

name: Shimei
bio: One of David’s mighty men who refused to acknowledge Adonijah as David’s successor (1 Kings 1:8). He is probably the same person who is called elsewhere (4:18) “the son of Elah.”

name: Shimei
bio: A Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:26, 27).

name: Shimei
bio: A Levite (2 Chr. 31:12, 13).

name: Shimrith
bio: The mother of Jehozabad, who murdered Joash (2 Kings 12:21); called also Shimrith, a Moabitess (2 Chr. 24:26).

name: Shobai
bio: Captors (Ezra 2:42).

name: Shuah
bio: One of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2; Chr. 1:32).

name: Shubael
bio: One of the sons of Heman; one of those whose duty it was to “lift up the horn” in the temple service (1 Chr. 25:4, 5); called also Shubael (ver. 20).

name: Simon
bio: One of the brothers of our Lord (Matt. 13:55; Mark 6:3).

name: Simon
bio: A leper of Bethany, in whose house Mary anointed our Lord’s head with ointment “as he sat at meat” (Matt. 26:6-13; Mark 14:3-9).

name: Sinite
bio: An inhabitant of Sin, near Arka (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15).

name: Sippai
bio: Extension, the son of the giant whom Sibbechai slew (2 Sam. 21:18); called also Sippai (1 Chr. 20:4).

name: Sisera
bio: The ancestor of some of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:53; Neh. 7:55).

name: Sopater
bio: The father who saves, probably the same as Sosipater, a kinsman of Paul (Rom. 16:21), a Christian of the city of Berea who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4-6).

name: Sosthenes
bio: Safe in strength, the chief ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, who was seized and beaten by the mob in the presence of Gallio, the Roman governor, when he refused to proceed against Paul at the instigation of the Jews (Acts 18:12-17).

name: Tabbaoth
bio: Impressions; rings, “the children of,” returned from the Captivity (Ezra 2:43).

name: Tahpenes
bio: The wife of Pharaoh, who gave her sister in marriage to Hadad the Edomite (1 Kings 11:19, 20).

name: Tanhumeth
bio: Consolation, a Netophathite; one of the captains who supported Gedaliah (2 Kings 25:23; Jer. 40:8).

name: Tarshish (son of Javan)
bio: One of the “sons” of Javan (Gen. 10:4; 1 Chr. 1:7).

name: Tartan
bio: One of Sennacherib’s messengers to Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:17).

name: Teresh
bio: Severe, a eunuch or chamberlain in the palace of Ahasuerus, who conspired with another to murder him. The plot was detected by Mordecai, and the conspirators were put to death (Esther 2:21; 6:2).

name: Tertullus
bio: A modification of “Tertius;” a Roman advocate, whom the Jews employed to state their case against Paul in the presence of Felix (Acts 24:1-9).

name: Theophilus
bio: Lover of God, a Christian, probably a Roman, to whom Luke dedicated both his Gospel (Luke 1:3) and the Acts of the Apostles (1:1). Nothing beyond this is known of him.

name: Tibni
bio: Building of Jehovah, the son of Ginath, a man of some position, whom a considerable number of the people chose as monarch. For the period of four years he contended for the throne with Omri (1 Kings 16:21, 22), who at length gained the mastery, and became sole monarch of Israel.

name: Tidal
bio: (in the LXX. called “Thorgal”), styled the “king of nations” (Gen. 14:1-9). Mentioned as Tudkhula on Arioch’s brick (see facing page 139). Goyyim, translated “nations,” is the country called Gutium, east of Tigris and north of Elam.

name: Timnah
bio: A “duke” or sheik of Edom (Gen. 36:40).

name: Tiras
bio: The youngest of the sons of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5).

name: Tirhakah
bio: The last king of Egypt of the Ethiopian (the fifteenth) dynasty. He was the brother-in-law of So (q.v.). He probably ascended the throne about B.C. 692, having been previously king of Ethiopia (2 Kings 19:9; Isa. 37:9), which with Egypt now formed one nation.

name: Unni
bio: A Levite whom David appointed to take part in bringing the ark up to Jerusalem from the house of Obed-edom by playing the psaltery on that occasion (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

name: Uriel
bio: A Kohathite ancestor of the prophet Samuel (1 Chr. 6:36).

name: Uriel
bio: The chief of the Kohathites at the time when the ark was brought up to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:5, 11).

name: Uz (son of Aram)
bio: The son of Aram, and grandson of Shem (Gen. 10:23; 1 Chr. 1:17).

name: Uz (son of Dishan)
bio: One of the Horite “dukes” in the land of Edom (Gen. 36:28).

name: Uzal
bio: A wanderer, a descendant of Joktan (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21), the founder apparently of one of the Arab tribes; the name also probably of the province they occupied and of their chief city.

name: Uzzi
bio: A grandson of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:2, 3).

name: Uzziel
bio: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4); called also Azareel (18).

name: Zabad
bio: The son of Shemath. He conspired against Joash, king of Judah, and slew him (2 Chr. 24:25, 26). He is called also Jozachar (2 Kings 12:21).

name: Zaccai
bio: Pure, one whose “sons” returned with Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:9; Neh. 7:14).

name: Zacher
bio: Memorial, a son of Jehiel (1 Chr. 8:31; 9:35); called Zechariah (9:37).

name: Zadok
bio: The father of Jerusha, who was wife of King Uzziah, and mother of King Jotham (2 Kings 15:33; 2 Chr. 27:1).

name: Zavan
bio: Terror, one of the “dukes of Edom” (Gen. 36:27); called also Zavan (1 Chr. 1:42).

name: Zechariah
bio: The father of Abijah, who was the mother of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:1).

name: Zelek
bio: Cleft, an Ammonite; one of David’s valiant men (2 Sam. 23:37).

name: Zemarite
bio: The designation of one of the Phoenician tribes (Gen. 10:18) who inhabited the town of Sumra, at the western base of the Lebanon range. In the Amarna tablets (B.C.

name: Zephaniah
bio: The father of Josiah, the priest who dwelt in Jerusalem when Darius issued the decree that the temple should be rebuilt (Zech. 6:10).

name: Zerah
bio: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 6:21, 41).

name: Zetham
bio: Olive planter, a Levite (1 Chr. 23:8).

name: Zibeon
bio: A Hivite (Gen. 36:2).

name: Zibiah
bio: The mother of King Joash (2 Kings 12:1; 2 Chr. 24:1).

name: Zichri
bio: A Levite, one of the sons of Asaph (Neh. 11:17); probably the same as Zichri (1 Chr. 9:15), and Zaccur (Neh. 12:35).

name: Zidon
bio: A fishery, a town on the Mediterranean coast, about 25 miles north of Tyre. It received its name from the “first-born” of Canaan, the grandson of Noah (Gen. 10:15, 19).

name: Ziha
bio: The name of a family of Nethinim (Ezra 2:43; Neh. 7:46).

name: Zimmah
bio: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 6:20).

name: Zimran
bio: Vine-dressers; celebrated, one of the sons of Abraham by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

name: Ziph
bio: A son of Jehaleleel (1 Chr. 4:16).

name: Zizah
bio: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 23:11).

name: Zohar
bio: The father of Ephron the Hittite (Gen. 23:8).

name: Zophah
bio: Spreading out, a son of Helem (1 Chr. 7:35), a chief of Asher.

name: Zur
bio: One of the five Midianite kings whom the Israelites defeated and put to death (Num. 31:8).

name: Zur
bio: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:30).

name: Abagtha
bio: One of the seven eunuchs in Ahasuerus’s court (Esther 1:10; 2:21).

name: Abda
bio: The father of Adoniram, whom Solomon set over the tribute (1 Kings 4:6); i.e., the forced labour (R.V., “levy”).

name: Abdeel
bio: Servant of God, (Jer. 36:26), the father of Shelemiah.

name: Abdi
bio: Ezra 10:26.

name: Abdiel
bio: Servant of God, (1 Chr. 5:15), a Gadite chief.

name: Abdon
bio: One of the “sons” of Shashak (1 Chr. 8:23). This is the name also of a Levitical town of the Gershonites, in the tribe of Asher (Josh. 21:30; 1 Chr. 6:74). The ruins of Abdeh, some 8 miles north-east of Accho, probably mark its site.

name: Abiah
bio: One of the sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8). “Abiah,” A.V.

name: Abiel (Arbathite)
bio: An Arbathite, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:32); called also Abi-albon (2 Sam. 23:31).

name: Abihail
bio: The second wife of King Rehoboam (2 Chr. 11:18), a descendant of Eliab, David’s eldest brother.

name: Abihud
bio: One of the sons of Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:3); called also Ahihud (ver. 7).

name: Abijah
bio: A son of Jeroboam, the first king of Israel. On account of his severe illness when a youth, his father sent his wife to consult the prophet Ahijah regarding his recovery.

name: Abinadab
bio: One of Solomon’s officers, who “provided victuals for the king and his household.” He presided, for this purpose, over the district of Dor (1 Kings 4:11).

name: Abiram
bio: The eldest son of Hiel the Bethelite, who perished prematurely in consequence of his father’s undertaking to rebuild Jericho (1 Kings 16:34), according to the words of Joshua (6:26).

name: Abishua
bio: The grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:4).

name: Abitub
bio: Father of goodness, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:11).

name: Abiud
bio: A descendant of Zerubbabel and father of Eliakim (Matt. 1:13, “Abiud”); called also Juda (Luke 3:26), and Obadiah (1 Chr. 3:21).

name: Achaicus
bio: (1 Cor. 16:17), one of the members of the church of Corinth who, with Fortunatus and Stephanas, visited Paul while he was at Ephesus, for the purpose of consulting him on the affairs of the church.

name: Addar
bio: Ample, splendid, son of Bela (1 Chr. 8:3); called also “Ard” (Gen. 46:21)

name: Addi
bio: Ornament, (Luke 3:28), the son of Cosam, and father of Melchi, one of the progenitors of Christ.

name: Adiel
bio: A family head of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:36).

name: Adina
bio: Slender, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:42), a Reubenite.

name: Adino
bio: The Eznite, one of David’s mighty men (2 Sam. 23:8).

name: Adnah
bio: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

name: Adnah
bio: A general under Jehoshaphat, chief over 300,000 men (2 Chr. 17:14).

name: Adonijah
bio: A Levite sent with the princes to teach the book of the law to the inhabitants of Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Adonijah
bio: One of the “chiefs of the people” after the Captivity (Neh. 10:16).

name: Adrammelech
bio: An idol; a form of the sun-god worshipped by the inhabitants of Sepharvaim (2 Kings 17:31), and brought by the Sepharvite colonists into Samaria.

name: Agag
bio: A king of the Amalekites referred to by Balaam (Num. 24:7). He lived at the time of the Exodus.

name: Agee
bio: Fugitive, the father of Shammah, who was one of David’s mighty men (2 Sam. 23:11)

name: Agur
bio: Gatherer; the collector, mentioned as author of the sayings in Prov. 30. Nothing is known of him beyond what is there recorded.

name: Ahiah
bio: One of Solomon’s secretaries (1 Kings 4:3).

name: Ahiah
bio: One of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 8:7, R.V.). In A.V. called “Ahiah.”

name: Ahiezer
bio: The chief of the Benjamite slingers that repaired to David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Ahihud
bio: Name different in Hebrew, meaning brother of Judah. Chief of the tribe of Asher; one of those appointed by Moses to superintend the division of Canaan among the tribe (Num. 34:27).

name: Ahihud
bio: A son of Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:7).

name: Ahijah
bio: One of the five sons of Jerahmeel, who was great-grandson of Judah (1 Chr. 2:25).

name: Ahijah
bio: A Pelonite, one of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:36); called also Eliam (2 Sam. 23:34).

name: Ahijah
bio: A Levite having charge of the sacred treasury in the temple (1 Chr. 26:20).

name: Ahimaaz
bio: The father Ahinoam, the wife of Saul (1 Sam. 14:50).

name: Ahiman
bio: One of the guardians of the temple after the Exile (1 Chr. 9:17).

name: Ahinadab
bio: Brother of liberality = liberal, one of the twelve commissariat officers appointed by Solomon in so many districts of his kingdom to raise supplies by monthly rotation for his household. He was appointed to the district of Mahanaim (1 Kings 4:14), east of Jordan.

name: Ahinoam
bio: The daughter of Ahimaaz, and wife of Saul (1 Sam. 14:50).

name: Ahio
bio: One of the sons of Beriah (1 Chr. 8:14).

name: Ahishar
bio: Brother of song = singer, the officer who was “over the household” of Solomon (1 Kings 4:6).

name: Ahoah
bio: Brotherly, one of the sons of Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:4). He is also called Ahiah (ver. 7) and Iri (1 Chr. 7:7). His descendants were called Ahohites (2 Sam. 23:9, 28).

name: Akkub
bio: A descendant of David (1 Chr. 3:24).

name: Akkub
bio: The head of one of the families of Nethinim (Ezra 2:45).

name: Alameth
bio: One of the nine sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8).

name: Alexander
bio: A man whose father, Simon the Cyrenian, bore the cross of Christ (Mark 15:21).

name: Alexander (Son of Simon)
bio: A relative of Annas the high priest, present when Peter and John were examined before the Sanhedrim (Acts 4:6).

name: Alexander (Jew of Ephesus)
bio: A Jew of Ephesus who took a prominent part in the uproar raised there by the preaching of Paul (Acts 19:33). The Jews put him forward to plead their cause before the mob.

name: Alphaeus
bio: The father of Levi, or Matthew (Mark 2:14).

name: Amariah
bio: A “chief priest” who took an active part in the reformation under Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 19:11); probably the same as mentioned in 1 Chr. 6:9.

name: Amariah
bio: One of the high priests in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 31:15).

name: Amariah
bio: Ezra 10:42.

name: Amariah
bio: Zeph. 1:1.

name: Amasa
bio: A son of Hadlai, and chief of Ephraim (2 Chr. 28:12) in the reign of Ahaz.

name: Amasai
bio: The leader of a body of men who joined David in the “stronghold,” probably of Adullam (1 Chr. 12:18).

name: Amasai
bio: One of the priests appointed to precede the ark with blowing of trumpets on its removal from the house of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Amasai
bio: The father of a Levite, one of the two Kohathites who took a prominent part at the instance of Hezekiah in the cleansing of the temple (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Amasiah
bio: Burden of (i.e., “sustained by”) Jehovah, the “son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself unto the Lord,” a captain over thousands under Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:16; comp. Judg. 5:9).

name: Amaziah
bio: The father of Joshah, one of the Simeonite chiefs in the time of Hezekiah (1 Chr. 4:34).

name: Amaziah
bio: A Levite, son of Hilkiah, of the descendants of Ethan the Merarite (1 Chr. 6:45).

name: Ammiel
bio: One of the twelve spies sent by Moses to search the land of Canaan (Num. 13:12). He was one of the ten who perished by the plague for their unfavourable report (Num. 14:37).

name: Ammiel
bio: One of the sons of Obed-edom the Levite (1 Chr. 26:5).

name: Ammihud
bio: The father of Talmai, king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after the murder of Amnon (2 Sam. 13:37).

name: Ammihud
bio: The son of Omri, and the father of Uthai (1 Chr. 9:4).

name: Ammizabad
bio: People of the giver, the son of Benaiah, who was the third and chief captain of the host under David (1 Chr. 27:6).

name: Amnon
bio: One of the sons of Shammai, of the children of Ezra (1 Chr. 4:20; comp. 17).

name: Amplias
bio: A Roman Christian saluted by Paul (Rom. 16:8).

name: Amram
bio: Ezra 10:34.

name: Anammelech
bio: One of the gods worshipped by the people of Sepharvaim, who colonized Samaria (2 Kings 17:31). The name means “Anu is king.” It was a female deity representing the moon, as Adrammelech (q.v.) was the male representing the sun.

name: Anan
bio: Cloud, one of the Israelites who sealed the covenant after the return from Babylon (Neh. 10:26).

name: Andronicus
bio: Man-conquering, a Jewish Christian, the kinsman and fellowprisoner of Paul (Rom. 16:7); “of note among the apostles.”

name: Anna
bio: Grace, an aged widow, the daughter of Phanuel. She was a “prophetess,” like Miriam, Deborah, and Huldah (2 Chr. 34:22). After seven years of married life her husband died, and during her long widowhood she daily attended the temple services.

name: Antipas
bio: A “faithful martyr” (Rev. 2:13), of whom nothing more is certainly known.

name: Apelles
bio: A Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:10), and styles “approved in Christ.”

name: Apollyon
bio: Destruction, the Hebrew name (equivalent to the Greek Apollyon, i.e., destroyer) of “the angel of the bottomless pit” (Rev. 9:11). It is rendered “destruction” in Job 28:22; 31:12; 26:6; Prov. 15:11; 27:20.

name: Apphia
bio: Increasing, a female Christian at Colosse (Philemon 1:2), supposed by some to have been the wife of Philemon.

name: Aram (son of Kemuel)
bio: The son of Shem (Gen. 10:22); according to Gen. 22:21, a grandson of Nahor. In Matt. 1:3, 4, and Luke 3:33, this word is the Greek form of Ram, the father of Amminadab (1 Chr. 2:10).

name: Archelaus
bio: Ruler of the people, son of Herod the Great, by Malthace, a Samaritan woman. He was educated along with his brother Antipas at Rome. He inherited from his father a third part of his kingdom viz., Idumea, Judea, and Samaria, and hence is called “king” (Matt. 2:22).

name: Ard
bio: Descent, a grandson of Benjamin (Num. 26:38-40). In 1 Chr. 8:3 he is called Addar. His descendants are mentioned in Num. 26:40.

name: Ardon
bio: Descendant, the last of the three sons of Caleb by his first wife Azubah (1 Chr. 2:18).

name: Aretas
bio: The father-in-law of Herod Antipas, and king of Arabia Petraea. His daughter returned to him on the occasion of her husband’s entering into an adulterous alliance with Herodias, the wife of Herod-Philip, his half-brother (Luke 3:19, 20; Mark 6:17; Matt. 14:3).

name: Arieh
bio: The lion, the name of one of the body-guard slain with Pekahiah at Samaria (2 Kings 15:25) by the conspirator Pekah.

name: Ariel
bio: One of the chief men sent by Ezra to procure Levites for the sanctuary (Ezra 8:16).

name: Armoni
bio: Inhabitant of a fortress, the first-named of the two sons of Saul and Rizpah. He was delivered up to the Gibeonites by David, and hanged by them (2 Sam. 21:8, 9).

name: Asaph
bio: The “keeper of the king’s forest,” to whom Nehemiah requested from Artaxerxes a “letter” that he might give him timber for the temple at Jerusalem (Neh. 2:8).

name: Ashpenaz
bio: The master of the eunuchs of Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:3), the “Rabsaris” of the court. His position was similar to that of the Kislar-aga of the modern Turkish sultans.

name: Asnappar
bio: Probably the same as Assur-bani-pal (Sardanapalos of the Greeks), styled the “great and noble” (Ezra 4:10), was the son and successor (B.C. 668) of Esar-haddon (q.v.).

name: Athaliah
bio: Ezra 8:7.

name: Azariah
bio: Son of Ethan, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:8).

name: Azariah
bio: The son of Oded, a remarkable prophet in the days of Asa (2 Chr. 15:1). He stirred up the king and the people to a great national reformation.

name: Azaziah
bio: One of the Levitical harpers in the temple (1 Chr. 15:21).

name: Azaziah
bio: The father of Hoshea, who was made ruler over the Ephraimites (1 Chr. 27:20).

name: Azaziah
bio: One who had charge of the temple offerings (2 Chr. 31:13).

name: Azmaveth
bio: An overseer over the royal treasury in the time of David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:25).

name: Azur
bio: The father of Hananiah, a false prophet (Jer. 28:1).

name: Azur
bio: The father of Jaazaniah (Ezek. 11:1).

name: Azzur
bio: One of those who sealed the covenant with Jehovah on the return from Babylon (Neh. 10:17).

name: Baalhanan
bio: An overseer of “the olive trees and sycomore trees in the low plains” (the Shephelah) under David (1 Chr. 27:28).

name: Baalis
bio: King of the Ammonites at the time of the Babylonian captivity (Jer. 40:14). He hired Ishmael to slay Gedaliah who had been appointed governor over the cities of Judah.

name: Baana
bio: One of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:12).

name: Baana
bio: Father of Zadok (Neh. 3:4).

name: Baanah
bio: Son of Hushai, another of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:16).

name: Bani
bio: One of David’s thirty-seven warriors, a Gadite (2 Sam. 23:36).

name: Bariah
bio: Fugitive, one of Shemaiah’s five sons. Their father is counted along with them in 1 Chr. 3:22.

name: Barsabas Justus
bio: Surnamed Barsabas (Acts 1:23); also called Justus. He was one of those who “companied with the apostles all the time that the Lord Jesus went out and in among them” (Acts 1:21), and was one of the candidates for the place of Judas.

name: Bartimaeus
bio: Son of Timaeus, one of the two blind beggars of Jericho (Mark 10:46; Matt. 20:30). His blindness was miraculously cured on the ground of his faith.

name: Barzillai
bio: A Meholathite, the father of Adriel (2 Sam. 21:8).

name: Bealiah
bio: Whose Lord is Jehovah, a Benjamite, one of David’s thirty heroes of the sling and bow (1 Chr. 12:5).

name: Bedan
bio: One of the judges of Israel (1 Sam. 12:11). It is uncertain who he was. Some suppose that Barak is meant, others Samson, but most probably this is a contracted form of Abdon (Judg. 12:13).

name: Beeri
bio: The father of Judith, one of the wives of Esau (Gen. 26:34), the same as Adah (Gen. 36:2).

name: Bela
bio: A son of Azaz (1 Chr. 5:8).

name: Benaiah
bio: The son of Jeiel (2 Chr. 20:14).

name: Bera
bio: Gift, or son of evil, king of Sodom at the time of the invasion of the four kings under Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2, 8, 17, 21).

name: Berachah
bio: One of the Benjamite warriors, Saul’s brethren, who joined David when at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Berechiah
bio: The fourth of the five sons of Zerubbabel, of the royal family of Judah (1 Chr. 3:20).

name: Berechiah
bio: One of the seven Ephraimite chieftains, son of Meshillemoth (2 Chr. 28:12).

name: Bered
bio: A son of Shuthelah, and grandson of Ephraim (1 Chr. 7:20).

name: Beriah
bio: A son of Ephraim (1 Chr. 7:20-23), born after the slaughter of his brothers, and so called by his father “because it went evil with his house” at that time.

name: Bezer
bio: A descendant of Asher (1 Chr. 7:37).

name: Bigtha
bio: Garden, or gift of fortune, one of the seven eunuchs or chamberlains who had charge of the harem of Ahasuerus (Esther 1:10).

name: Bilgah
bio: The head of the fifteenth sacerdotal course for the temple service (1 Chr. 24:14).

name: Birsha
bio: Son of wickedness, a king of Gomorrah whom Abraham succoured in the invasion of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2).

name: Blastus
bio: Chamberlain to king Herod Agrippa I. (Acts 12:20). Such persons generally had great influence with their masters.

name: Buz
bio: The second son of Nahor and Milcah, and brother of Huz (Gen. 22:21). Elihu was one of his descendants (Job 32:2).

name: Buz
bio: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Gad (1 Chr. 5:14).

name: Cainan (son of Arphaxad)
bio: The son of Arphaxad (Luke 3:36). He is nowhere named in the Old Testament. He is usually called the “second Cainan.”

name: Calcol
bio: (1 Chr. 2:6), sustenance, the same probably as Chalcol (1 Kings 4:31), one of the four sages whom Solomon excelled in wisdom; for “he was wiser than all men.”

name: Candace
bio: The queen of the Ethiopians whose “eunuch” or chamberlain was converted to Christianity by the instrumentality of Philip the evangelist (Acts 8:27). The country which she ruled was called by the Greeks Meroe, in Upper Nubia.

name: Chenaanah
bio: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 7:10).

name: Chesed
bio: Gain, the son of Nahor (Gen. 22:22).

name: Chloe
bio: Verdure, a female Christian (1 Cor. 1:11), some of whose household had informed Paul of the divided state of the Corinthian church. Nothing is known of her.

name: Claudia
bio: A female Christian mentioned in 2 Tim. 4:21. It is a conjecture having some probability that she was a British maiden, the daughter of king Cogidunus, who was an ally of Rome, and assumed the name of the emperor, his patron, Tiberius Claudius, and that she was the wife of Pudens.

name: Claudius Lysias
bio: Claudius Lysias, a Greek who, having obtained by purchase the privilege of Roman citizenship, took the name of Claudius (Acts 21:31-40; 22:28; 23:26).

name: Clement
bio: Mild, a Christian of Philippi, Paul’s “fellow-labourer,” whose name he mentions as “in the book of life” (Phil. 4:3).

name: Conaniah
bio: Whom Jehovah hath set, a Levite placed over the tithes brought into the temple (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Coz
bio: A descendant of Judah. 1 Chr. 4:8, “Coz;” R.V., “Hakkoz.”

name: Crescens
bio: Increasing, probably one of the seventy disciples of Christ. He was one of Paul’s assistants (2 Tim. 4:10), probably a Christian of Rome.

name: Cyrenius
bio: The Grecized form of Quirinus. His full name was Publius Sulpicius Quirinus. Recent historical investigation has proved that Quirinus was governor of Cilicia, which was annexed to Syria at the time of our Lord’s birth.

name: Damaris
bio: A heifer, an Athenian woman converted to Christianity under the preaching of Paul (Acts 17:34). Some have supposed that she may have been the wife of Dionysius the Areopagite.

name: Darda
bio: Pearl of wisdom, one of the four who were noted for their wisdom, but whom Solomon excelled (1 Kings 4:31).

name: Darius
bio: Darius the Persian (Neh. 12:22) was probably the Darius II. (Ochus or Nothus) of profane history, the son of Artaxerxes Longimanus, who was the son and successor of Ahasuerus (Xerxes). There are some, however, who think that the king here meant was Darius III.

name: Debir
bio: The king of Eglon, one of the five Canaanitish kings who were hanged by Joshua (Josh. 10:3, 23) after the victory at Gibeon. These kings fled and took refuge in a cave at Makkedah.

name: Delaiah
bio: The head of the twenty-third division of the priestly order (1 Chr. 24:18).

name: Diblaim
bio: Doubled cakes, the mother of Gomer, who was Hosea’s wife (Hos. 1:3).

name: Dionysius
bio: The Areopagite, one of Paul’s converts at Athens (Acts 17:34).

name: Dodo
bio: A descendant of Issachar (Judg. 10:1).

name: Drusilla
bio: Third and youngest daughter of Herod Agrippa I. (Acts 12:1-4, 20-23). Felix, the Roman procurator of Judea, induced her to leave her husband, Azizus, the king of Emesa, and become his wife.

name: Eber (a Benjamite)
bio: The oldest of the three sons of Elpaal the Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:12).

name: Eber (Amok Family Head)
bio: The head of the priestly family of Amok in the time of Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:20).

name: Eden
bio: Son of Joah, and one of the Levites who assisted in reforming the public worship of the sanctuary in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Ehud
bio: A descendant of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:10), his great-grandson.

name: Elah
bio: The second of the three sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh (1 Chr. 4:15).

name: Elasah
bio: The son of Shaphan, one of the two who were sent by Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar, and also took charge of Jeremiah’s letter to the captives in Babylon (Jer. 29:3).

name: Eleazar
bio: An inhabitant of Kirjath-jearim who was “sanctified” to take charge of the ark, although not allowed to touch it, while it remained in the house of his father Abinadab (1 Sam. 7:1, 2; comp. Num. 3:31; 4:15).

name: Eleazar
bio: A son of Phinehas associated with the priests in taking charge of the sacred vessels brought back to Jerusalem after the Exile (Ezra 8:33).

name: Eliab
bio: One of the Gadite heroes who joined David in his stronghold in the wilderness (1 Chr. 12:9).

name: Eliada
bio: A mighty man of war, a Benjamite (2 Chr. 17:17).

name: Eliadah
bio: An Aramite of Zobah, captain of a marauding band that troubled Solomon (1 Kings 11:23).

name: Eliakim
bio: The son of Abiud, of the posterity of Zerubbabel (Matt. 1:13).

name: Eliakim
bio: The son of Melea (Luke 3:30), and probably grandson of Nathan.

name: Eliam
bio: This name also occurs as that of a Gilonite, the son of Ahithophel, and one of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:34). perhaps these two were the same person.

name: Eliashib
bio: A priest, head of one of the courses of the priests of the time of David (1 Chr. 24:12).

name: Elidad
bio: Whom God has loved, son of Chislon, and chief of the tribe of Benjamin; one of those who were appointed to divide the Promised Land among the tribes (Num. 34:21).

name: Eliel
bio: A chief of Manasseh, on the east of Jordan (1 Chr. 5:24).

name: Eliel
bio: A Gadite who joined David in the hold at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:11).

name: Eliel
bio: One of the overseers of the offerings in the reign of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 31:13).

name: Eliezer (Abraham's Steward)
bio: “Of Damascus,” the “steward” (R.V., “possessor”) of Abraham’s house (Gen. 15:2, 3). It was probably he who headed the embassy sent by Abraham to the old home of his family in Padan-aram to seek a wife for his son Isaac. The account of this embassy is given at length in Gen. 24.

name: Eliezer
bio: The son of Becher, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8).

name: Eliezer
bio: One of the priests who blew the trumpet before the ark when it was brought to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Eliezer
bio: Son of Zichri, and chief of the Reubenites under David (1 Chr. 27:16).

name: Eliezer
bio: A prophet in the time of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 20:37). Others of this name are mentioned Luke 3:29; Ezra 8:16; 10:18, 23, 31.

name: Elihu
bio: One of the captains of thousands of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

name: Elihu
bio: One of the family of Obed-edom, who were appointed porters of the temple under David (1 Chr. 26:7).

name: Elika
bio: God is his rejector, one of David’s thirty-seven distinguished heros (2 Sam. 23:25).

name: Eliphelet
bio: One of David’s distinguished warriors (2 Sam. 23:34); called also Eliphal in 1 Chr. 11:35.

name: Eliphelet
bio: A descendant of king Saul through Jonathan (1 Chr. 8:39).

name: Elishama
bio: A priest sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the people the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Elishaphat
bio: Whom God has judged, one of the “captains of hundreds” associated with Jehoiada in the league to overthrow the usurpation of Athaliah (2 Chr. 23:1).

name: Elisheba
bio: God is her oath, the daughter of Amminadab and the wife of Aaron (Ex. 6:23).

name: Epaenetus
bio: Commendable, a Christian at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutation (Rom. 16:5). He is spoken of as “the first fruits of Achaia” (R.V., “of Asia”, i.e., of proconsular Asia, which is probably the correct reading).

name: Ephah
bio: 1 Chr. 2:46, a concubine of Caleb.

name: Ephah
bio: 1 Chr. 2:47, a descendant of Judah. Ephah, a word of Egyptian origin, meaning measure; a grain measure containing “three seahs or ten omers,” and equivalent to the bath for liquids (Ex. 16:36; 1 Sam. 17:17; Zech. 5:6). The double ephah in Prov.

name: Epher
bio: The head of one of the families of trans-Jordanic Manasseh who were carried captive by Tiglath-pileser (1 Chr. 5:24).

name: Ethan
bio: “The Ezrahite,” distinguished for his wisdom (1 Kings 4:31). He is named as the author of the 89th Psalm. He was of the tribe of Levi.

name: Ethbaal
bio: With Baal, a king of Sidon (B.C. 940-908), father of Jezebel, who was the wife of Ahab (1 Kings 16:31). He is said to have been also a priest of Astarte, whose worship was closely allied to that of Baal, and this may account for his daughter’s zeal in promoting idolatry in Israel…

name: Euodias
bio: A good journey, a female member of the church at Philippi. She was one who laboured much with Paul in the gospel. He exhorts her to be of one mind with Syntyche (Phil. 4:2). From this it seems they had been at variance with each other.

name: Eutychus
bio: Fortunate, (Acts 20:9-12), a young man of Troas who fell through drowsiness from the open window of the third floor of the house where Paul was preaching, and was “taken up dead.” The lattice-work of the window being open to admit the air, the lad fell out and down to the court b…

name: Ezer
bio: A Levite (Neh. 3:19).

name: Ezri
bio: Help of Jehovah, the son of Chelub. He superintended, under David, those who “did the work of the field for tillage” (1 Chr. 27:26).

name: Fortunatus
bio: Fortunate, a disciple of Corinth who visited Paul at Ephesus, and returned with Stephanas and Achaicus, the bearers of the apostle’s first letter to the Corinthians (1 Cor. 16:17).

name: Gaddi
bio: Fortunate, the representative of the tribe of Manasseh among the twelve “spies” sent by Moses to spy the land (Num. 13:11).

name: Gaddiel
bio: Fortune (i.e., sent) of God, the representative of the tribe of Zebulum among the twelve spies (Num. 13:10).

name: Gaius (of Macedonia)
bio: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14).

name: Gaius (of Derbe)
bio: A man of Derbe who accompanied Paul into Asia on his last journey to Jerusalem

name: Gaius
bio: A Christain of Asia Minor to whom John addressed his third epistle (3 John 1:1).

name: Gamul
bio: Weaned the leader of one of the priestly courses (1 Chr. 24:17).

name: Geber
bio: A valiant man, (1 Kings 4:19), one of Solomon’s purveyors, having jurisdiction over a part of Gilead, comprising all the kingdom of Sihon and part of the kingdom of Og (Deut. 2; 31).

name: Gedaliah
bio: One of the Jewish nobles who conspired against Jeremiah (Jer. 38:1).

name: Gemariah
bio: The son of Hilkiah, who accompanied Shaphan with the tribute-money from Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar, and was the bearer at the same time of a letter from Jeremiah to the Jewish captives at Babylon (Jer. 29:3, 4).

name: Genubath
bio: Theft, the son of Hadad, of the Edomitish royal family. He was brought up in Pharaoh’s household. His mother was a sister of Tahpenes, the king of Egypt’s wife, mentioned in 1 Kings 11:20.

name: Gershom
bio: The son of Manasseh (Judg. 18:30), in R.V. “of Moses.”

name: Gershom
bio: A descendant of Phinehas who returned with Ezra from Babylon (Ezra 8:2).

name: Gog
bio: A Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:4), the father of Shimei.

name: Hadlai
bio: Resting, an Ephraimite; the father of Amasa, mentioned in 2 Chr. 28:12.

name: Hakkoz
bio: The thorn, the head of one of the courses of the priests (1 Chr. 24:10).

name: Hammoleketh
bio: The queen, the daughter of Machir and sister of Gilead (1 Chr. 7:17, 18). Abiezer was one of her three children.

name: Hanan
bio: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:23).

name: Hanan
bio: One of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:43).

name: Hanan
bio: One of the chiefs who subscribed the covenant (Neh. 10:22).

name: Hananiah
bio: A chief of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:24).

name: Hananiah
bio: One of Uzziah’s military officers (2 Chr. 26:11).

name: Hananiah
bio: Ezra 10:28.

name: Hananiah
bio: The “ruler of the palace; he was a faithful man, and feared God above many” (Neh. 7:2).

name: Hananiah
bio: A priest, son of Jeremiah (Neh. 12:12).

name: Hananiah
bio: Grandfather of the captain who arrested Jeremiah (Jer. 37:13).

name: Haniel
bio: A chief of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:39).

name: Hanniel
bio: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 34:23).

name: Haran (son of Caleb)
bio: The son of Caleb of Judah (1 Chr. 2:46) by his concubine Ephah.

name: Harbona
bio: (a Persian word meaning “ass-driver”), one of the seven eunuchs or chamberlains of king Ahasuerus (Esther 1:10; 7:9).

name: Harhaiah
bio: Zeal of Jehovah, (Neh. 3:8) “of the goldsmiths,” one whose son helped to repair the wall of Jerusalem.

name: Harnepher
bio: A chief of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:36).

name: Harum
bio: Elevated, (1 Chr. 4:8), a descendant of Judah.

name: Haruz
bio: Eager, the father of Meshullemeth, the wife of king Manasseh (2 Kings 21:19) and mother of king Amon.

name: Hasadiah
bio: Favoured by Jehovah, one of the sons of Pedaiah (1 Chr. 3:20), of the royal line of David.

name: Hasenuah
bio: Bristling or hated, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 9:7).

name: Hashabiah
bio: One of the chief Levites (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Hashabiah
bio: A Levite (Neh. 11:22).

name: Hashabniah
bio: One of the Levites whom Ezra appointed to interpret the law to the people (Neh. 9:5).

name: Hashbadana
bio: Consideration in judging, stood at Ezra’s left hand when he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Hashubah
bio: Ibid., a descendant of David (1 Chr. 3:20).

name: Hashum
bio: Stood on Ezra’s left hand while he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Hathath
bio: Terror, son of Othniel (1 Chr. 4:13).

name: Hattush
bio: Ezra 8:2.

name: Hazo
bio: Vision, one of the sons of Nahor (Gen. 22:22).

name: Heber
bio: One of the seven heads of the families of the Gadites (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Heber
bio: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:17).

name: Helez
bio: One of Judah’s posterity (1 Chr. 2:39).

name: Heli
bio: Elevation, father of Joseph in the line of our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:23).

name: Helkai
bio: Smooth-tongued, one of the chief priests in the time of Joiakim (Neh. 12:15).

name: Heman
bio: 1 Kings 4:31; 1 Chr. 2:6, a son of Zerah, noted for his wisdom.

name: Heman
bio: 1 Kings 4:31; 1 Chr. 2:6, a son of Zerah, noted for his wisdom.

name: Hepher
bio: The second son of Asher (1 Chr. 4:6).

name: Hepher
bio: One of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:36).

name: Hermes
bio: Mercury, a Roman Christian (Rom. 16:14).

name: Hermogenes
bio: Mercury-born, at one time Paul’s fellow-labourer in Asia Minor, who, however, afterwards abandoned him, along with one Phygellus, probably on account of the perils by which they were beset (2 Tim. 1:15).

name: Herodion
bio: A Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes and calls his “kinsman” (Rom. 16:11).

name: Hezion
bio: Vision, the father of Tabrimon, and grandfather of Ben-hadad, king of Syria (1 Kings 15:18).

name: Hezir
bio: The head of the seventeenth course of the priests (1 Chr. 24:15).

name: Hezir
bio: Neh. 10:20, one who sealed Nehemiah’s covenant.

name: Hiel
bio: Life of (i.e., from) God, a native of Bethel, who built (i.e., fortified) Jericho some seven hundred years after its destruction by the Israelites. There fell on him for such an act the imprecation of Joshua (6:26).

name: Hizkijah
bio: (Neh. 10:17), one who sealed the covenant.

name: Hodijah
bio: Neh. 10:18, a Levite who sealed the covenant.

name: Hoham
bio: Jehovah impels, the king of Hebron who joined the league against Gibeon. He and his allies were defeated (Josh. 10:3, 5, 16-27).

name: Hoshea
bio: 1 Chr. 27:20. The ruler of Ephraim in David’s time.

name: Iddo
bio: Timely. The father of Ahinadab, who was one of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:14).

name: Iddo
bio: Lovely. The son of Zechariah (1 Chr. 27:21), the ruler of Manasseh in David’s time.

name: Igal
bio: Num. 13:7, one of the spies of the tribe of Issachar.

name: Igal
bio: Son of Nathan of Zobah, and one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:36).

name: Immer
bio: The father of Zadok (Neh. 3:29).

name: Iphedeiah
bio: Set free by Jehovah, a chief of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:25).

name: Ira
bio: A Jairite and priest, a royal chaplain (2 Sam. 20:26) or confidential adviser (comp. 2 Sam. 8:18; 1 Chr. 18:17).

name: Irad
bio: Runner; wild ass, one of the antediluvian patriarchs, the father of Mehujael (Gen. 4:18), and grandson of Cain.

name: Iscah
bio: Spy, the daughter of Haran and sister of Milcah and Lot (Gen. 11:29, 31).

name: Ishbi-benob
bio: My seat at Nob, one of the Rephaim, whose spear was three hundred shekels in weight. He was slain by Abishai (2 Sam. 21:16, 17).

name: Ishmaiah
bio: Son of Obadiah, and viceroy of Zebulun under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:19).

name: Ismaiah
bio: A Gibeonite who joined David at Ziklag, “a hero among the thirty and over the thirty” (1 Chr. 12:4).

name: Jaakobah
bio: Heel-catcher, a form of the name Jacob, one of the descendants of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:36).

name: Jaanai
bio: Mourner, one of the chief Gadites (1 Chr. 5:12).

name: Jaasiel
bio: Made by God, one of David’s body-guard, the son of Abner (1 Chr. 27:21), called Jasiel in 1 Chr. 11:47.

name: Jaazaniah
bio: The son of Jeremiah, and one of the chief Rechabites (Jer. 35:3).

name: Jaazaniah
bio: The son of Shaphan (Ezek. 8:11).

name: Jabal
bio: A stream, a descendant of Cain, and brother of Jubal; “the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle” (Gen. 4:20). This description indicates that he led a wandering life.

name: Jabin
bio: A king of Hazor, at the time of the entrance of Israel into Canaan (Josh. 11:1-14), whose overthrow and that of the northern chief with whom he had entered into a confederacy against Joshua was the crowning act in the conquest of the land (11:21-23; comp. 14:6-15).

name: Jachan
bio: Mourner, one of the chief Gadite “brothers” in Bashan (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Jachin
bio: The head of one of the courses (the twenty-first) of priests (1 Chr. 24:17).

name: Jaddua
bio: One of the chiefs who subscribed the covenant (Neh. 10:21).

name: Jadon
bio: Judge, a Meronothite who assisted in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:7).

name: Jahath
bio: One of the sons of Shelomoth, of the family of Kohath (1 Chr. 24:22).

name: Jahath
bio: A Levite of the family of Merari, one of the overseers of the repairs of the temple under Josiah (2 Chr. 34:12).

name: Jahaziel
bio: A priest who accompanied the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 16:6).

name: Jahaziel
bio: The son of Zechariah, a Levite of the family of Asaph (2 Chr. 20:14-17). He encouraged Jehoshaphat against the Moabites and Ammonites.

name: Jahdai
bio: Grasper, a descendant of Caleb, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:47).

name: Jahzerah
bio: Returner, the son of Meshullam, and father of Adiel (1 Chr. 9:12).

name: Jair
bio: A Benjamite, the father of Mordecai, Esther’s uncle (Esther 2:5).

name: Jakeh
bio: Pious, the father of Agur (Prov. 30:1). Nothing is known of him.

name: Jakim
bio: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:19).

name: Jakim
bio: Chief of the twelfth priestly order (1 Chr. 24:12).

name: Jalon
bio: Lodger, the last of the four sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

name: Jambres
bio: One of those who opposed Moses in Egypt (2 Tim. 3:8).

name: Jannes
bio: One of the Egyptians who “withstood Moses” (2 Tim. 3:8).

name: Japhia
bio: The king of Lachish, who joined in the confederacy against Joshua (Josh. 10:3), and was defeated and slain. In one of the Amarna tablets he speaks of himself as king of Gezer. Called also Horam (Josh. 10:33).

name: Jarib
bio: One of the chiefs sent by Ezra to bring up the priests to Jerusalem (Ezra 8:16).

name: Jarib
bio: Ezra 10:18.

name: Jashen
bio: Sleeping, called also Hashem (1 Chr. 11:34); a person, several of whose sons were in David’s body-guard (2 Sam. 23:32).

name: Jashub
bio: Ezra 10:29.

name: Jedaiah
bio: Invoker of Jehovah. The son of Shimri, a chief Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:37).

name: Jedaiah
bio: One of those who repaired the walls of Jerusalem after the return from Babylon (Neh. 3:10).

name: Jediael
bio: A Shimrite, one of David’s bodyguard (1 Chr. 11:45). Probably same as in 12:20.

name: Jediael
bio: A Korhite of the family of Ebiasaph, and one of the gate-keepers to the temple (1 Chr. 26:2).

name: Jehaleleel
bio: A descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 4:16).

name: Jehalelel
bio: A Levite of the family of Merari (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Jehdeiah
bio: One of the Levitical attendants at the temple, a descendant of Shubael (1 Chr. 24:20).

name: Jehdeiah
bio: A Meronothite, herdsman of the asses under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:30).

name: Jehiel
bio: One of David’s guard (1 Chr. 11:44).

name: Jehiel
bio: A Hachmonite, a tutor in the family of David toward the close of his reign (1 Chr. 27:32).

name: Jehiel
bio: The second of Jehoshaphat’s six sons (2 Chr. 21:2).

name: Jehiel
bio: One of the Levites of the family of Heman who assisted Hezekiah in his work of reformation (2 Chr. 29:14).

name: Jehiel
bio: A “prince” and “ruler of the house of God” who contributed liberally to the renewal of the temple sacrifices under Josiah (2 Chr. 35:8).

name: Jehiel
bio: The father of Obadiah (Ezra 8:9).

name: Jehizkiah
bio: Jehovah strengthens, one of the chiefs of Ephraim (2 Chr. 28:12).

name: Jehohanan
bio: A Korhite, the head of one of the divisions of the temple porters (1 Chr. 26:3).

name: Jehohanan
bio: One of Jehoshaphat’s “captains” (2 Chr. 17:15).

name: Jehoiarib
bio: Jehovah defends, a priest at Jerusalem, head of one of the sacerdotal courses (1 Chr. 9:10; 24:7). His “course” went up from Babylon after the Exile (Ezra 2:36-39; Neh. 7:39-42).

name: Jehonathan
bio: One of the stewards of David’s store-houses (1 Chr. 27:25).

name: Jehonathan
bio: A Levite who taught the law to the people of Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Jehoram
bio: A priest sent by Jehoshaphat to instructruct the people in Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Jehoshaphat
bio: Solomon’s purveyor in Issachar (1 Kings 4:17).

name: Jehoshaphat
bio: One of the priests who accompanied the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Jehozabad
bio: The son of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4), one of the Levite porters.

name: Jehu
bio: The son of Obed, and father of Azariah (1 Chr. 2:38).

name: Jehu
bio: One of the Benjamite slingers that joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Jeiel
bio: 1 Chr. 5:7. A Reubenite chief.

name: Jeiel
bio: 2 Chr. 26:11. A scribe.

name: Jeiel
bio: 2 Chr. 29:13. A Levite of the sons of Asaph.

name: Jeiel
bio: One of the chief Levites, who made an offering for the restoration of the Passover by Josiah (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Jeiel
bio: Ezra 8:13.

name: Jeiel
bio: Ezra 10:43.

name: Jemima
bio: Dove, the eldest of Job’s three daughters born after his time of trial (Job 42:14).

name: Jephunneh
bio: One of the descendants of Asher (1 Chr. 7:38).

name: Jerahmeel
bio: The son of Kish, a Levite (1 Chr. 24:29).

name: Jerahmeel
bio: Son of Hammelech (Jer. 36:26).

name: Jered
bio: A son of Ezra probably (1 Chr. 4:18).

name: Jeremiah
bio: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Manasseh on the east of Jordan (1 Chr. 5:24).

name: Jeremiah
bio: A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:4).

name: Jeremiah
bio: A Gadite who joined David in the wilderness (1 Chr. 12:10).

name: Jeremiah
bio: A Gadite warrior (1 Chr. 12:13).

name: Jerimoth
bio: One of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 7:7).

name: Jerimoth
bio: A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

name: Jerimoth
bio: 1 Chr. 27:19, ruler of Naphtali.

name: Jerimoth
bio: One of David’s sons (2 Chr. 11:18).

name: Jerimoth
bio: A Levite, one of the overseers of the temple offerings (2 Chr. 31:13) in the reign of Hezekiah.

name: Jeroham
bio: 1 Chr. 9:8; a Benjamite.

name: Jeroham
bio: 1 Chr. 12:7; a Benjamite.

name: Jeroham
bio: The father of Azareel, the “captain” of the tribe of Dan (1 Chr. 27:22).

name: Jeroham
bio: 2 Chr. 23:1; one whose son assisted in placing Joash on the throne.

name: Jerubbesheth
bio: Contender with the shame; i.e., idol, a surname also of Gideon (2 Sam. 11:21).

name: Jesaiah
bio: One of the three sons of Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:21).

name: Jeshaiah
bio: Son of Athaliah (Ezra 8:7).

name: Jeshebeab
bio: Seat of his father, the head of the fourteenth division of priests (1 Chr. 24:13).

name: Jesher
bio: Uprightness, the first of the three sons of Caleb by Azubah (1 Chr. 2:18).

name: Jeshua
bio: A Levite appointed by Hezekiah to distribute offerings in the priestly cities (2 Chr. 31:15).

name: Jeshua
bio: A Levite (Ezra 8:33).

name: Jeshua
bio: Son of Kadmiel (Neh. 12:24).

name: Jesus
bio: A Jewish Christian surnamed Justus (Col. 4:11). Je’sus, the proper, as Christ is the official, name of our Lord. To distinguish him from others so called, he is spoken of as “Jesus of Nazareth” (John 18:7), and “Jesus the son of Joseph” (John 6:42).

name: Jether
bio: The oldest of Gideon’s seventy sons (Judg. 8:20).

name: Jether
bio: 1 Chr. 2:32; one of Judah’s posterity.

name: Jeuel
bio: Snatched away by God, a descendant of Zerah (1 Chr. 9:6).

name: Jeush
bio: A son of Bilhan, grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:10).

name: Jeush
bio: One of the three sons of Rehoboam (2 Chr. 11:19).

name: Jeziel
bio: Assembled by God, a son of Azmaveth. He was one of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Joah
bio: One of the sons of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4), a Korhite porter.

name: Joah
bio: Son of Joahaz, and “recorder” (q.v.) or keeper of the state archives under King Josiah (2 Chr. 34:8).

name: Joahaz
bio: (2 Chr. 34:8), a contracted form of Jehoahaz (q.v.).

name: Joanna
bio: The grandson of Zerubbabel, in the lineage of Christ (Luke 3:27); the same as Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:19).

name: Joash
bio: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Joash
bio: One who had charge of the royal stores of oil under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:28).

name: Jobab
bio: A Canaanitish king (Josh. 11:1) who joined the confederacy against Joshua.

name: Joel
bio: One of David’s famous warriors (1 Chr. 11:38).

name: Joelah
bio: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:7).

name: Joezer
bio: Jehovah is his help, one of the Korhites who became part of David’s body-guard (1 Chr. 12:6).

name: Johanan
bio: The oldest of King Josiah’s sons (1 Chr. 3:15).

name: Johanan
bio: One of the Gadite heroes who joined David in the desert of Judah (1 Chr. 12:12).

name: John (Relative of the High Priest)
bio: One who, with Annas and Caiaphas, sat in judgment on the apostles Peter and John (Acts 4:6). He was of the kindred of the high priest; otherwise unknown.

name: Joiarib
bio: Ezra 8:16, a “man of understanding” whom Ezra sent to “bring ministers for the house of God.”

name: Joiarib
bio: Neh. 11:5; a descendant of Judah.

name: Jokim
bio: Whom Jehovah has set up, one of the descendants of Shelah (1 Chr. 4:22).

name: Jonathan
bio: A Levite descended from Gershom (Judg. 18:30). His history is recorded in 17:7-13 and 18:30. The Rabbins changed this name into Manasseh “to screen the memory of the great lawgiver from the stain of having so unworthy an apostate among his near descendants.” He became priest of t…

name: Josabad
bio: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:4).

name: Joseph (son of Judah)
bio: The son of Judah, and father of Semei (Luke 3:26). Other two of the same name in the ancestry of Christ are also mentioned (3:24, 30).

name: Jubal
bio: Jubilee, music, Lamech’s second son by Adah, of the line of Cain. He was the inventor of “the harp” (Heb. kinnor, properly “lyre”) and “the organ” (Heb. ‘ugab, properly “mouth-organ” or Pan’s pipe), Gen. 4:21.

name: Juda
bio: The father of Simeon in Christ’s maternal ancestry (Luke 3:30).

name: Judas (of Galilee)
bio: the Graecized form of Judah.

name: Judas (Jew of Damascus)
bio: A Jew of Damascus (Acts 9:11), to whose house Ananias was sent. The street called “Straight” in which it was situated is identified with the modern “street of bazaars,” where is still pointed out the so-called “house of Judas.”

name: Julia
bio: A Christian woman at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutations (Rom. 16:15), supposed to be the wife of Philologus.

name: Junia
bio: (Rom. 16:7), a Christian at Rome to whom Paul sends salutations along with Andronicus.

name: Justus
bio: A Jewish proselyte at Corinth, in whose house, next door to the synagogue, Paul held meetings and preached after he left the synagogue (Acts 18:7).

name: Kemuel
bio: The third son of Nahor (Gen. 22:21).

name: Kemuel
bio: Son of Shiphtan, appointed on behalf of the tribe of Ephraim to partition the land of Canaan (Num. 34:24).

name: Kemuel
bio: A Levite (1 Chr. 27:17).

name: Kenaz
bio: Caleb’s grandson (1 Chr. 4:15).

name: Keren-happuch
bio: Horn of the face-paint = cosmetic-box, the name of Job’s third daughter (Job. 42:14), born after prosperity had returned to him.

name: Kish
bio: A Levite in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Kish
bio: The great-grandfather of Mordecai (Esther 2:5).

name: Kore
bio: A Levitical porter at the east gate of the temple (2 Chr. 31:14).

name: Lapidoth
bio: Torches. Deborah is called “the wife of Lapidoth” (Judg. 4:4). Some have rendered the expression “a woman of a fiery spirit,” under the supposition that Lapidoth is not a proper name, a woman of a torch-like spirit.

name: Leummim
bio: Peoples; nations, the last mentioned of the three sons of Dedan, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:3).

name: Levi
bio: Luke 3:24.

name: Levi
bio: The father of Matthat, and son of Simeon, of the ancestors of Christ (Luke 3:29).

name: Lo-ammi
bio: Not my people, a symbolical name given by God’s command to Hosea’s second son in token of Jehovah’s rejection of his people (Hos. 1:9, 10), his treatment of them as a foreign people. This Hebrew word is rendered by “not my people” in ver. 10; 2:23.

name: Lois
bio: The maternal grandmother of Timothy. She is commended by Paul for her faith (2 Tim. 1:5).

name: Lucifer
bio: Brilliant star, a title given to the king of Babylon (Isa. 14:12) to denote his glory.

name: Lysanias
bio: Tetrarch of Abilene (Luke 3:1), on the eastern slope of Anti-Lebanon, near the city of Damascus.

name: Maachah
bio: The father of Hanan, who was one of David’s body-guard (1 Chr. 11:43).

name: Maaseiah
bio: One of the “captains of hundreds” associated with Jehoiada in restoring king Jehoash to the throne (2 Chr. 23:1).

name: Maaseiah
bio: One who was sent by king Josiah to repair the temple (2 Chr. 34:8). He was governor (Heb. sar, rendered elsewhere in the Authorized Version “prince,” “chief captain,” chief ruler”) of Jerusalem.

name: Maath
bio: Small, a person named in our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:26).

name: Maaziah
bio: The head of the twenty-fourth priestly course (1 Chr. 24:18) in David’s reign.

name: Mahalaleel
bio: Neh. 11:4, a descendant of Perez.

name: Mahalath
bio: The daughter of Jerimoth, who was one of David’s sons. She was one of Rehoboam’s wives (2 Chr. 11:18).

name: Mahath
bio: Another Kohathite Levite, of the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Mahol
bio: Dance, the father of four sons (1 Kings 4:31) who were inferior in wisdom only to Solomon.

name: Malachi
bio: Messenger or angel, the last of the minor prophets, and the writer of the last book of the Old Testament canon (Mal. 4:4, 5, 6). Nothing is known of him beyond what is contained in his book of prophecies.

name: Malchiah
bio: A priest who stood by Ezra when he “read in the book of the law of God” (Neh. 8:4).

name: Malchijah
bio: The head of the fifth division of the priests in the time of David (1 Chr. 24:9).

name: Malchijah
bio: One of the priests appointed as musicians to celebrate the completion of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:42).

name: Malchus
bio: Reigning, the personal servant or slave of the high priest Caiaphas. He is mentioned only by John. Peter cut off his right ear in the garden of Gethsemane (John 18:10). But our Lord cured it with a touch (Matt. 26:51; Mark 14:47; Luke 22:51).

name: Malluch
bio: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 6:44).

name: Malluch
bio: Ezra 10:29.

name: Malluch
bio: Ezra 10:32

name: Manaen
bio: Consoler, a Christian teacher at Antioch. Nothing else is known of him beyond what is stated in Acts 13:1, where he is spoken of as having been brought up with (Gr. syntrophos; rendered in R.V.

name: Mary (Mother of John Mark)
bio: Mary the mother of John Mark was one of the earliest of our Lord’s disciples. She was the sister of Barnabas (Col. 4:10), and joined with him in disposing of their land and giving the proceeds of the sale into the treasury of the Church (Acts 4:37; 12:12).

name: Mary (of Rome)
bio: A Christian at Rome who treated Paul with special kindness (Rom. 16:6).

name: Mattan
bio: The father of Shephatiah (Jer. 38:1).

name: Mattaniah
bio: A Levite who assisted in purifying the temple at the reformation under Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:13).

name: Mattathias
bio: The son of Amos, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:25).

name: Mattathias
bio: The son of Semei, in the same genealogy (Luke 3:26).

name: Matthan
bio: The son of Eleazar, and father of Jacob, who was the father of Joseph, the husband of the Virgin Mary (Matt. 1:15).

name: Matthat
bio: The son of Levi, and father of Heli (Luke 3:24).

name: Matthat
bio: Son of another Levi (Luke 3:29).

name: Mattithiah
bio: The eldest son of Shallum, of the family of Korah (1 Chr. 9:31).

name: Mattithiah
bio: One who stood by Ezra while reading the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Mehetabeel
bio: Whose benefactor is God, the father of Delaiah, and grandfather of Shemaiah, who joined Sanballat against Nehemiah (Neh. 6:10).

name: Mehujael
bio: Smitten by God, the son of Irad, and father of Methusael (Gen. 4:18).

name: Mehuman
bio: Faithful, one of the eunchs whom Ahasuerus (Xerxes) commanded to bring in Vashti (Esther 1:10).

name: Melchi
bio: Luke 3:24.

name: Melchi
bio: The son of Addi, and father of Neri (Luke 3:28).

name: Melea
bio: Fulness, the son of Menan and father of Eliakim, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

name: Mephibosheth
bio: The name of Saul’s son by the concubine Rizpah (q.v.), the daughter of Aiah. He and his brother Armoni were with five others “hanged on a hill before the Lord” by the Gibeonites, and their bodies exposed in the sun for five months (2 Sam. 21:8-10).

name: Meraiah
bio: Resistance, a chief priest, a contemporary of the high priest Joiakim (Neh. 12:12).

name: Merodach-baladan
bio: Merodach has given a son, (Isa. 39:1), “the hereditary chief of the Chaldeans, a small tribe at that time settled in the marshes at the mouth of the Euphrates, but in consequence of his conquest of Babylon afterwards, they became the dominant caste in Babylonia itself.” One beari…

name: Mesha
bio: Heb. id, a king of Moab, the son of Chemosh-Gad, a man of great wealth in flocks and herds (2 Kings 3:4). After the death of Ahab at Ramoth-Gilead, Mesha shook off the yoke of Israel;

name: Mesha
bio: Heb. meysh’a, “deliverance,” the eldest son of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:42), and brother of Jerahmeel.

name: Meshillemoth
bio: The father of Berechiah (2 Chr. 28:12).

name: Meshullam
bio: Grandfather of Shaphan, “the scribe,” in the reign of Josiah (2 Kings 22:3).

name: Meshullam
bio: One of the chief Gadites in Bashan in the time of Jotham (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Meshullam
bio: One of the principal Israelites who supported Ezra when expounding the law to the people (Neh. 8:4).

name: Meshullam
bio: A chief priest (Neh. 12:16).

name: Meshullemeth
bio: Friend, the wife of Manasseh, and the mother of Amon (2 Kings 21:19), Kings of Judah.

name: Methusael
bio: Champion of El; man of God, a descendant of Cain (Gen. 4:18), so called, perhaps, to denote that even among the descendants of Cain God had not left himself without a witness.

name: Mibhar
bio: Choice, a Hagarene, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:38); called also Bani the Gadite (2 Sam. 23:36).

name: Mibsam
bio: A son of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:25).

name: Micah
bio: A descendant of Joel the Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:5).

name: Michael
bio: The father of Sethur, the spy selected to represent Asher (Num. 13:13).

name: Michael
bio: A chief Gadite in Bashan (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Michael
bio: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 6:40).

name: Michael
bio: 1 Chr. 7:3, a chief of the tribe of Issachar.

name: Michael
bio: 1 Chr. 8:16, a Benjamite.

name: Michael
bio: A Manassite, “a captain of thousands” who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

name: Michael
bio: The father of Omri (1 Chr. 27:18).

name: Michael
bio: One of the sons of king Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 21:2, 4). He was murdered by his brother Jehoram.

name: Michaiah
bio: One of those sent out by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people in the law (2 Chr. 17:7).

name: Michaiah
bio: A priest (Neh. 12:41).

name: Michri
bio: Prize of Jehovah, a Benjamite, the father of Uzzi (1 Chr. 9:8).

name: Mikloth
bio: An officer under Dodai, in the time of David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:4).

name: Milalai
bio: Eloquent, a Levitical musician (Neh. 12:36) who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem.

name: Miriam
bio: 1 Chr. 4:17, one of the descendants of Judah.

name: Misham
bio: Their cleansing or their beholding, a Benjamite, one of the sons of Elpaal (1 Chr. 8:12).

name: Mishmannah
bio: Fatness, one of the Gadite heroes who gathered to David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:10).

name: Mithredath
bio: The “treasurer” of King Cyrus (Ezra 1:8).

name: Mnason
bio: Reminding, or remembrancer, a Christian of Jerusalem with whom Paul lodged (Acts 21:16). He was apparently a native of Cyprus, like Barnabas (11:19, 20), and was well known to the Christians of Caesarea (4:36).

name: Moza
bio: One of the sons of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:46).

name: Naam
bio: Pleasantness, one of the three sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh (1 Chr. 4:15).

name: Naamah (line of Cain)
bio: The daughter of Lamech and Zillah (Gen. 4: 22).

name: Naarai
bio: Youthful, a military chief in David’s army (1 Chr. 11:37), called also Paarai (2 Sam. 23:35).

name: Nahash
bio: The father of Amasa, who was commander-in-chief of Abasolom’s army (2 Sam. 17:25). Jesse’s wife had apparently been first married to this man, to whom she bore Abigail and Zeruiah, who were thus David’s sisters, but only on the mother’s side (1 Chr. 2:16).

name: Nahath
bio: A Levite, one of the overseers of the sacred offerings of the temple (2 Chr. 31:13).

name: Nahbi
bio: Hidden, one of the twelve spies sent out to explore the land of Canaan (Num. 13:14).

name: Narcissus
bio: Daffodil, a Roman whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:11). He is supposed to have been the private secretary of the emperor Claudius. This is, however, quite uncertain.

name: Nathan
bio: A prophet in the reigns of David and Solomon (2 Chr. 9:29). He is first spoken of in connection with the arrangements David made for the building of the temple (2 Sam. 7:2, 3, 17), and next appears as the reprover of David on account of his sin with Bathsheba (12:1-14).

name: Nathan
bio: Ezra 8:16.

name: Nebushasban
bio: Adorer of Nebo, or Nebo saves me, the “Rabsaris,” or chief chamberlain, of the court of Babylon. He was one of those whom the king sent to release Jeremiah from prison in Jerusalem (Jer. 39:13).

name: Nedabiah
bio: Moved of Jehovah, one of the sons of Jeconiah (1 Chr. 3:18).

name: Nehushta
bio: Copper, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem, and the wife of Jehoiakin (2 Kings 24:8), king of Judah.

name: Nemuel
bio: A Reubenite, a son of Eliab, and brother of Dathan and Abiram (Num. 26:9).

name: Nethaneel
bio: One of David’s brothers (1 Chr. 2:14).

name: Nethaneel
bio: A priest who blew the trumpet before the ark when it was brought up to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Nethaneel
bio: A temple porter, of the family of the Korhites (1 Chr. 26:4).

name: Nethaneel
bio: One of the “princes” appointed by Jehoshaphat to teach the law through the cities of Judah (2 Chr. 17:7).

name: Nethaneel
bio: A chief Levite in the time of Josiah (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Nethaneel
bio: Ezra 10:22.

name: Nethaneel
bio: A priest’s son who bore a trumpet at the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:36).

name: Nethaniah
bio: A Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Nicanor
bio: Conqueror, one of the seven deacons appointed in the apostolic Church (Acts 6:1-6). Nothing further is known of him.

name: Nicolas
bio: The victory of the people, a proselyte of Antioch, one of the seven deacons (Acts 6:5).

name: Noadiah
bio: A Levite who returned from Babylon (Ezra 8:33).

name: Noadiah
bio: A false prophetess who assisted Tobiah and Sanballat against the Jews (Neh. 6:14). Being bribed by them, she tried to stir up discontent among the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and so to embarrass Nehemiah in his great work of rebuilding the ruined walls of the city.

name: Obadiah
bio: A chief of the tribe of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:3).

name: Obadiah
bio: A Gadite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:9).

name: Obadiah
bio: A prince of Zebulun in the time of David (1 Chr. 27:19).

name: Obadiah
bio: One of the princes sent by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people in the law (2 Chr. 17:7).

name: Obadiah
bio: A Levite who superintended the repairs of the temple under Josiah (2 Chr. 34:12).

name: Obadiah
bio: One who accompanied Ezra on the return from Babylon (Ezra 8:9).

name: Obil
bio: A keeper of camels, an Ishmaelite who was “over the camels” in the time of David (1 Chr. 27:30).

name: Oded
bio: A prophet in the time of Ahaz and Pekah (2 Chr. 28:9-15).

name: Ohel
bio: A house; tent, the fourth son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:20).

name: Olympas
bio: A Roman Christian whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:15).

name: Ophrah
bio: A fawn. 1 Chr. 4:14.

name: Oren
bio: Ash or pine, the son of Jerahmeel (1 Chr. 2:25).

name: Othni
bio: A lion of Jehovah, a son of Shemaiah, and one of the temple porters in the time of David (1 Chr. 26:7). He was a “mighty man of valour.”

name: Ozem
bio: One of David’s brothers; the sixth son of Jesse (1 Chr. 2:15).

name: Ozem
bio: A son of Jerahmeel (1 Chr. 2:25).

name: Paarai
bio: Opening of the Lord, “the Arbite,” one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:35); called also Naarai, 1 Chr. 11:37.

name: Palti
bio: Deliverance from the Lord, one of the spies representing the tribe of Benjamin (Num. 13:9).

name: Paltiel
bio: Deliverance of God, the prince of Issachar who assisted “to divide the land by inheritance” (Num. 34:26).

name: Parmashta
bio: Strong-fisted, a son of Haman, slain in Shushan (Esther 9:9).

name: Parmenas
bio: Constant, one of the seven “deacons” (Acts 6:5).

name: Parshandatha
bio: An interpreter of the law, the eldest of Haman’s sons, slain in Shushan (Esther 9:7).

name: Paruah
bio: Flourishing, the father of Jehoshaphat, appointed to provide monthly supplies for Solomon from the tribe of Issachar (1 Kings 4:17).

name: Pasach
bio: Clearing, one of the sons of Japhlet, of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:33).

name: Patrobas
bio: A Christian at Rome to whom Paul sent salutations (Rom. 16:14).

name: Pedahel
bio: Redeemed of God, the son of Ammihud, a prince of Naphtali (Num. 34:28).

name: Pedaiah
bio: The father of Zebudah, who was the wife of Josiah and mother of king Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:36).

name: Pedaiah
bio: . The father of Joel, ruler of the half-tribe of Manasseh (1 Chr. 27:20).

name: Pelaiah
bio: One of David’s posterity (1 Chr. 3:24).

name: Pelatiah
bio: A son of Hananiah and grandson of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:21).

name: Pelet
bio: A descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 2:47).

name: Pelet
bio: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Peleth
bio: A Reubenite whose son was one of the conspirators against Moses and Aaron (Num. 16:1).

name: Peleth
bio: One of the sons of Jonathan (1 Chr. 2:33).

name: Persis
bio: A female Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:12). She is spoken of as “beloved,” and as having “laboured much in the Lord.”

name: Pethahiah
bio: The chief of one of the priestly courses (the nineteenth) in the time of David (1 Chr. 24:16).

name: Pethahiah
bio: A Levite (Ezra 10:23).

name: Pethahiah
bio: A descendant of Judah who had some office at the court of Persia (Neh. 11:24).

name: Pethuel
bio: Vision of God, the father of Joel the prophet (Joel 1:1).

name: Peulthai
bio: Wages of the Lord, one of the sons of Obed-edom, a Levite porter (1 Chr. 26:5).

name: Phanuel
bio: Face of God, father of the prophetess Anna (q.v.), Luke 2:36.

name: Pharaoh
bio: The Pharaoh of 1 Chr. 4:18.

name: Phebe
bio: A “deaconess of the church at Cenchrea,” the port of Corinth. She was probably the bearer of Paul’s epistle to the Romans. Paul commended her to the Christians at Rome; “for she hath been,” says he, “a succourer of many, and of myself also” (Rom. 16:1, 2).

name: Philemon
bio: An inhabitant of Colosse, and apparently a person of some note among the citizens (Col. 4:9; Philemon 1:2). He was brought to a knowledge of the gospel through the instrumentality of Paul (19), and held a prominent place in the Christian community for his piety and beneficence (4…

name: Philetus
bio: Amiable, with Hymenaeus, at Ephesus, said that the “resurrection was past already” (2 Tim. 2:17, 18). This was a Gnostic heresy held by the Nicolaitanes.

name: Phlegon
bio: Burning, a Roman Christian to whom Paul sent salutations (Rom. 16:14).

name: Phygellus
bio: Fugitive, a Christian of Asia, who “turned away” from Paul during his second imprisonment at Rome (2 Tim. 1:15). Nothing more is known of him.

name: Puah
bio: One of the two midwives who feared God, and refused to kill the Hebrew male children at their birth (Ex. 1:15-21).

name: Puah
bio: A descendant of Issachar (Judg. 10:1).

name: Pudens
bio: Bashful, a Christian at Rome, who sent his greetings to Timothy (2 Tim. 4:21).

name: Quartus
bio: Fourth, a Corinthian Christian who sent by Paul his salutations to friends at Rome (Rom. 16:23).

name: Rabsaris
bio: Chief of the Heads, one of the three officers whom Sennacherib sent from Lachish with a threatening message to Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:17; Jer. 39:3, 13).

name: Rachab
bio: '=Rahab, a name found in the genealogy of our Lord (Matt. 1:5).

name: Raham
bio: Merciful, one of the descendants of Caleb, the son of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:44).

name: Ram
bio: A person mentioned in Job 32:2 as founder of a clan to which Elihu belonged. The same as Aram of Gen. 22:21.

name: Raphu
bio: Healed, a Benjamite, whose son Palti was one of the twelve spies (Num. 13:9).

name: Regem-melech
bio: Friend of the king, one of the two messengers sent by the exiled Jews to Jerusalem in the time of Darius (Zech. 7:2) to make inquiries at the temple.

name: Rehum
bio: A Levite (Neh. 3:17).

name: Rei
bio: Friendly, one who maintained true allegiance to king David (1 Kings 1:8) when Adonijah rebelled.

name: Rephael
bio: Healed of God, one of Shemaiah’s sons. He and his brethren, on account of their “strength for service,” formed one of the divisions of the temple porters (1 Chr. 26:7, 8).

name: Rezon
bio: Prince, son of Eliadah. Abandoning the service of Hadadezer, the king of Zobah, on the occasion of his being defeated by David, he became the “captain over a band” of marauders, and took Damascus, and became king of Syria (1 Kings 11:23-25; 2 Sam. 8:3-8).

name: Rhesa
bio: Affection, son of Zorobabel, mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:27).

name: Rhoda
bio: A rose, the damsel in the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark. She came to hearken when Peter knocked at the door of the gate (Acts 12:12-15).

name: Sacar
bio: A son of Obed-edom the Gittite, and a temple porter (1 Chr. 26:4).

name: Sadoc
bio: Just, mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Matt. 1:14).

name: Salathiel
bio: Whom I asked of God, the son of Jeconiah (Matt. 1:12; 1 Chr. 3:17); also called the son of Neri (Luke 3:27). The probable explanation of the apparent discrepancy is that he was the son of Neri, the descendant of Nathan, and thus heir to the throne of David on the death of Jeconia…

name: Sallai
bio: A Benjamite (Neh. 11:8).

name: Samgar-nebo
bio: Be gracious, O Nebo! or a cup-bearer of Nebo, probably the title of Nergal-sharezer, one of the princes of Babylon (Jer. 39:3).

name: Sapphira
bio: Beautiful, the wife of Ananias (q.v.). She was a partner in his guilt and also in his punishment (Acts 5:1-11).

name: Sceva
bio: An implement, a Jew, chief of the priests at Ephesus (Acts 19:13-16); i.e., the head of one of the twenty-four courses of the house of Levi. He had seven sons, who “took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus,” in imitation of Paul.

name: Secundus
bio: Second, a Christian of Thessalonica who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4).

name: Segub
bio: The youngest son of Hiel the Bethelite. His death is recorded in 1 Kings 16:34 (comp. Josh. 6:26).

name: Semei
bio: Mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:26).

name: Seorim
bio: Barley, the chief of the forth priestly course (1 Chr. 24:8).

name: Seraiah
bio: The grandfather of Jehu (1 Chr. 4:35).

name: Sergius Paulus
bio: A “prudent man” (R.V., “man of understanding”), the deputy (R.V., “proconsul”) of Cyprus (Acts 13:6-13). He became a convert to Christianity under Paul, who visited this island on his first mission to the heathen.

name: Sethur
bio: Hidden, one of the spies sent to search the Promised Land. He was of the tribe of Asher (Num. 13:13).

name: Shaashgaz
bio: Servant of the beautiful, a chief eunuch in the second house of the harem of king Ahasuerus (Esther 2:14).

name: Shallum
bio: A descendant of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:25).

name: Shallum
bio: An Ephraimite chief (2 Chr. 28:12).

name: Shallum
bio: The uncle of the prophet Jeremiah (Jer. 32:7).

name: Shamir
bio: One of the sons of Michah (1 Chr. 24:24).

name: Shammah
bio: One of David’s three mighty men (2 Sam. 23:11, 12).

name: Shammua
bio: One of the spies sent out by Moses to search the land (Num. 13:4). He represented the tribe of Reuben.

name: Shaphat
bio: One of the spies. He represented the tribe of Simeon (Num. 13:5).

name: Shaphat
bio: One of David’s chief herdsmen (1 Chr. 27:29).

name: Shebaniah
bio: A Levite appointed to blow the trumpet before the ark of God (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Shebaniah
bio: A priest (Neh. 10:12).

name: Shecaniah
bio: A priest to whom the tenth lot came forth when David divided the priests (1 Chr. 24:11).

name: Shecaniah
bio: One of the priests who were set “to give to their brethren by courses” of the daily portion (2 Chr. 31:15). Shechani’ah, id.

name: Shechaniah
bio: Ezra 8:5.

name: Shechaniah
bio: The father-in-law of Tobiah (Neh. 6:18).

name: Shelemiah
bio: Ezra 10:39.

name: Shelemiah
bio: The father of Hananiah (Neh. 3:30).

name: Shelemiah
bio: Father of a captain of the ward (Jer. 37:13).

name: Shema
bio: A Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:8).

name: Shema
bio: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:13).

name: Shema
bio: One who stood by Ezra when he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Shemaah
bio: Rumour, a Benjamite whose sons “came to David to Ziklag” (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Shemaiah
bio: A Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:37).

name: Shemaiah
bio: A Levite (1 Chr. 24:6).

name: Shemaiah
bio: One of the Levites whom Jehoshaphat appointed to teach the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Shemaiah
bio: A Levite (2 Chr. 29:14).

name: Shemaiah
bio: A Levite appointed to “distribute the oblations of the Lord” (2 Chr. 31:15).

name: Shemaiah
bio: A Levite (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Shemaiah
bio: A false prophet who hindered the rebuilding of Jerusalem (Neh. 6:10).

name: Shemaiah
bio: A priest (Neh. 12:42).

name: Shemaiah
bio: The father of Urijah the prophet (Jer. 26:20).

name: Shemaiah
bio: The father of a prince in the reign of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:12).

name: Shemariah
bio: One who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

name: Shemeber
bio: Soaring on high, the king of Zeboiim, who joined with the other kings in casting off the yoke of Chedorlaomer. After having been reconquered by him, he was rescued by Abraham (Gen. 14:2).

name: Shemiramoth
bio: A Levite in the reign of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Shemuel
